summaries.summary: The adapter boundary proper is in good shape — provider SDK/home/SQLite access is tightly enforced by tests/architecture/adapter-boundary.test.ts plus duplicated ESLint rules, and src/core facades (content-dir, settings, logger, execution-ledger) are clean pure re-exports with no drift. The real architectural debt is one layer up: the `runtime.config.get()/replace()` whole-config surface lets plugins (models, team) hardcode OpenClaw's config schema while completely bypassing the carefully-built raw-config allowlist/audit gate; the workflows plugin's registries are load-bearing core infrastructure imported statically by the plugin loader; and the images plugin imports assets internals directly despite assets registering the equivalent hooks. A secondary theme is doc-vs-reality drift: src/lib hosts server-only side-effectful modules despite being documented client-safe, and the published SDK's implementations actually live in an undocumented src/components/ tree with a package-to-app circular dependency.

Bakin's architecture is mostly disciplined — adapter boundaries are real and test-enforced — but the audit found three structural debts: a 17-cycle runtime circular-dependency cluster centered on the exec-tool registry (which itself lives in the wrong layer, scripts/lib/), one explicit violation of the documented core↔plugin HookRegistry boundary inside the plugin loader, and a Next.js-era residue layer (src/types, src/components/calendar, plugin-slot) carrying both dead code and a 4-way drifted Task type duplicated across store, SDK, plugin, and legacy layers. Dead code is modest (~620 LOC across seven verified-unreachable files) because most leftovers are stale exports inside live files rather than whole dead modules; every dead-code claim was verified against all alias forms, dynamic imports, scripts, the release pipeline, and docs surfaces, and one initially-suspect file (src/cli/schedule.ts) was confirmed alive and excluded.

The CLI is mid-migration and stalled: a tested, registry-driven runner framework (src/core/cli/{parser,options,runner,result}.ts) was built to replace the 4,632-line hand-rolled switch in cli/bakin.ts but has zero production callers, leaving two entry points glued together by process.exit/argv monkey-patching with circular delegation between them. Output rendering is the biggest duplication: ~50 identical printXxxTui wrapper functions and 155 inline isTTY branches across three files, all funneling into one 2,808-line readonly.tsx. The two CLIs genuinely disagree on shared concerns — no-arg behavior (start vs help), `update` (works in binary, advertised-but-rejected via the npm bin), and BAKIN_URL (honored everywhere except the third CLI module src/cli/schedule.ts). Consolidating into src/core/cli/ with one file per command group, one HTTP client, and one render helper kills roughly 1,500+ lines and the entire class of divergence bugs; the compiled binary already bundles both CLIs, so there is no build-side obstacle.

The asset-serving and plugin/agent-package install paths are well-hardened: the versioned asset server (plugins/assets/lib/serve.ts + asset-id.ts) funnels every request through `isValidAssetId`/`assetDirRelPath` which reject separators and `..`; the plugin asset catch-all (api/plugins/assets.ts) guards `..` and a strict pluginId regex; plugin install (api/plugins/install.ts) realpath-contains local sources and re-confirms github subpath containment; both the Whiskit artifact extractor (src/core/whiskit/artifact.ts) and the uninstall-snapshot restore (src/core/plugins/uninstall-snapshot.ts) validate the tar listing for absolute/`..`/symlink entries before extraction (no zip-slip); and agent-package contribution source paths are containment-checked in package-integrity.ts. The one confirmed gap is the agent avatar endpoint, which joins an unvalidated query `id` directly into a path (P1, limited impact due to a fixed `avatar.jpg` suffix). A secondary defense-in-depth nit is the plugin-settings route skipping id validation (P2, no exploitable traversal because Node normalizes the URL pathname).

The production plugin and agent-package install/upgrade pipeline is well-hardened: github fetches use argv-array `git` with `--` end-of-options (src/core/github-source-cache.ts, src/core/plugins/upgrade.ts), refs are validated against `/^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$/` (packages/core/src/plugins/source.ts), local sources are realpath-contained to ~/.bakin/$HOME/cwd, dependency installs run `bun install --ignore-scripts` so postinstall scripts never execute (src/core/whiskit/build.ts:164), build subprocesses use an env allowlist, and permissioned installs gate behind a signed consent token bound to the manifest sha. OpenClaw dispatch (execFileAsync + argv), the git worktree plugin, and the assets ffmpeg call are all argv-based with no shell interpolation. The one concrete injection is in dead legacy code (src/core/plugin-installer.ts) that is still tested and thus re-adoptable; a secondary supply-chain gap is that github installs trust a prebuilt dist/ that is never rebuilt from the import-validated source.

The secret-handling posture is genuinely strong: provider API keys are isolated in a dedicated ~/.bakin/secrets.json written 0600 with an env override, the GET /api/secrets endpoint is write-only/masked (returns only which providers have a key, never values), no plugin settingsSchema stores secrets, settings/antfly logging logs keys/urls but never values, and SSE never carries settings or secret payloads. I found no live credential leakage into logs, audit.jsonl, search, SSE, error responses, or settings GET. SSRF surfaces are limited to operator/provider-controlled URLs (antfly settings URL, image-provider response URLs, github clone/whiskit downloads) with no attacker-controlled internal-fetch-and-read-back path. The three findings are invariant drift and latent risk, all P2: the antfly basic-auth password rides settings.json (contradicting the secret-store's own 'never in a settings export' invariant), the execution ledger persists up-to-500-char image prompts in idempotency.result_json (contradicting 'coordination facts only, never content'), and a dead-code installFromGithub helper builds a git clone via shell string interpolation (unreachable today but a loaded gun).

SDK adoption is genuinely good — PluginHeader, BakinDrawer, EmptyState, FacetFilter, AgentAvatar, and the ui primitives are used consistently across all 10 plugins, so the big list-page/drawer patterns are NOT duplicated. The debt sits in the gaps the SDK never filled: time/duration formatting (7 local reimplementations including a byte-identical copy of formatAge in the health plugin), confirm-delete dialogs (6 hand-rolled copies), the cancelled-flag JSON-fetch effect (11 copies), and a missing plugin-event subscription primitive that pushed the assets plugin into opening three raw EventSource connections without reconnect. One within-plugin inconsistency (team's local EmptyState shadowing the SDK one) and a recurring tone-badge styling idiom round it out; all five strong clusters have a clear SDK export home (@makinbakin/sdk/utils, /components, /hooks).

Bakin's route layer is in mid-migration: a capable shared dispatcher (packages/core/src/routing) exists, but the team and workflows plugins plus the host package-management handlers still hand-roll validation, body parsing, and error envelopes, leaving the legacy param-injection shim duplicated in two places and three competing error-envelope dialects. The strongest debt clusters are storage-shaped: a canonical atomicWriteJson with only 4 consumers while 7+ files re-implement tmp+rename writes, plugin-settings read/write spread across five sites with diverging change-notification side effects, and one frontmatter regex copied into 10 files (including 3 verbatim parseSkillFile copies and 4 drifting lesson parsers). The per-request PluginContext in the plugin catch-all is a near-copy of the registry's ctx factory and has already drifted (missing onSettingsChange). All findings have 2+ real consumers and obvious homes in packages/core; none require provider-boundary changes.

The hard boundary is in good shape: zero plugin client files import from packages/host/src or use @/* aliases, and plugin server code's relative reaches into src/core are app-internal core-plugin idiom rather than SDK gaps. The real debt is concentrated in two places: (1) packages/sdk/src/types is a hand-maintained parallel declaration of the entire plugin contract from packages/core/src/plugin-types.ts with no parity enforcement, no in-repo consumers for the contract types, and already-observable drift (AvailableModel, WorkflowInstance's id-vs-instanceId mismatch); (2) missing client data primitives — no SSE event-subscription hook (forcing the assets plugin into three parallel EventSource connections and the host store into hardcoded per-plugin bump counters) and no data hooks for the two cross-plugin REST dependencies that 2+ plugins hand-fetch (models catalog, workflow definitions). Smaller dividends: an EmptyState fork and two families of duplicated date formatters that exist only because the SDK versions are missing one feature each.

The build/release path (build-plugins → build-vendors → build-host-shell → generate-embedded-assets → build-binary) is in good shape: errors propagate (every step checks exit codes or throws, with CI gates like assert-production-assets and required-asset checks), and the instance rig is carefully sandboxed under dev/. The real debt is duplication that has already started to drift: the externals contract is hardcoded in two build entry points despite externals.ts existing precisely because that duplication broke plugins before, the core-plugin list exists in three copies (dev.ts already silently omits 'images'), and scripts/docs/check.ts validates generate.ts output using copy-pasted renderers that have diverged. The 2,585-line docs generator needs seams, its hook/slot docs are regex-scraped rather than registry-derived (the one place docs can drift from the server), and scripts/lib/ is actually production runtime code masquerading as build tooling — plus dev/imitation-crab seeding code verifiably ships inside the compiled release binary.

confirmed.title: images plugin imports assets plugin internals directly, bypassing the HookRegistry
confirmed.evidence: plugins/images/lib/tools.ts:6-8 — `import { getAsset, listAssets, upsertFromSource, resolveStoreFile } from '../../assets/lib/asset-service'`, `import { isValidAssetId } from '../../assets/lib/asset-id'`, plus `AssetManifest`/`AssetVersion` types from '../../assets/lib/manifest'. CLAUDE.md (Plugin Communication) states cross-plugin calls go exclusively through the HookRegistry with 'No direct imports between plugins', and the assets plugin actually registers the equivalent hooks (plugins/assets/index.ts:407-448: assets.listByTask, assets.resolveServe, assets.saveFromSource, assets.purgeClipboardForTask) — images sidesteps them with relative imports into the sibling plugin's lib/. This also bypasses the plugin-permission layer (src/lib/plugin-permissions.ts gates ctx.* surfaces, not raw module imports) even though images declares assets.read/assets.write in its manifest. This is the only plugin-to-plugin import in the repo (verified by sweep across all 10 plugins).
confirmed.recommendation: Route images' asset writes/reads through the existing assets.* hooks (extend assets.saveFromSource / add an assets.upsertFromSource hook for the manifest-returning path), or promote asset-service into packages/core if it is genuinely shared infrastructure. Then add a guard (see guard-gap finding) so the pattern cannot recur.

verdict.reasoning: Every cited fact verified by reading the files. plugins/images/lib/tools.ts:6-8 directly imports getAsset/listAssets/upsertFromSource/resolveStoreFile from ../../assets/lib/asset-service, isValidAssetId from ../../assets/lib/asset-id, and manifest types — used as real value imports at lines 229, 235, 244, 379-399, 442, 452. The rule it violates is explicit: CLAUDE.md Plugin Communication and .claude/knowledge/plugin-system.md:1118 ("No direct imports between plugins or from core → plugins"). The assets plugin does register the sanctioned hooks at plugins/assets/index.ts:407-448 (assets.listByTask, assets.getAssetTypes, assets.resolveServe, assets.saveFromSource, assets.purgeClipboardForTask). My independent sweep confirms images→assets is the only sibling-plugin import in plugins/** (all other ../../ imports target src/core or packages/core). The permission-bypass claim also holds: src/lib/plugin-permissions.ts:64-68,233 gates only ctx.assets method calls via wrapObject, and upsertFromSource/listAssets/resolveStoreFile are not even on the gated AssetsAPI (packages/core/src/plugin-types.ts:631-639), so the raw imports sidestep the declared assets.read/assets.write grants. Mitigations keep this at P1 rather than P0: images declares dependencies:["assets","models"] in its manifest; the assets watcher self-heals indexing and emits asset.changed on any manifest write (plugins/assets/index.ts:329-346), so direct upsertFromSource causes no data loss; and core plugins are statically bundled so nothing breaks at runtime today. One nuance for the fix: neither ctx.assets nor the existing hooks cover everything images needs (filtered listAssets, manifest-returning upsert, resolveStoreFile), and core itself dynamic-imports plugins/assets/lib/asset-service to implement ctx.assets (src/lib/plugin-context-services.ts:133-146) — evidence that promoting asset-service into packages/core is the structurally honest remedy, exactly as the finding's second recommendation suggests.

confirmed.title: runtime.config.get()/update()/replace() is an ungated whole-provider-config surface that nullifies the raw-config governance
confirmed.evidence: packages/core/src/adapters/runtime/concepts.ts:447-452 defines RuntimeConfigAccess with `get<T>()` (no reason, no key), `update(patch)` (no reason), and `replace(next, reason)`. The OpenClaw impl (packages/adapter-openclaw/src/runtime.ts:1033-1063) returns the ENTIRE provider config from get() with no audit, while raw() is the one gated by the allowlist+audit machinery in src/core/runtime-config-raw.ts:19-50 — get() is strictly more powerful than the raw('*') read that is allowlisted only for onboarding. Consumers hardcode OpenClaw's config schema outside the adapter: plugins/models/index.ts:33-54 declares RuntimeModelConfig mirroring OpenClaw's `agents.defaults.model.primary`/`agents.list[].subagents.model` shape and does whole-config read-modify-replace (index.ts:84-98); plugins/team/index.ts:216-219 reads `agents.defaults.model.primary`; src/core/openclaw-integration.ts:41-71 rewrites `mcp.servers` and replaces the full config. The architecture test only denies `config\.raw|\.raw<` outside the gate (tests/architecture/adapter-boundary.test.ts:79-82), so all of this passes the boundary check. A whole-config replace() from the models plugin can also clobber concurrent provider-config changes since it round-trips the entire file.
confirmed.recommendation: Promote the real use cases to typed adapter methods (e.g. runtime.models.getAssignments()/setAgentModel(), runtime.mcp.syncServers()) so provider config shape stays inside packages/adapter-openclaw, and have update() do targeted deep-merge patches instead of full replace(). Either delete get()/replace() from the contract or fold them into the runtime-config-raw allowlist+audit gate, and extend the adapter-boundary denylist to cover `config.get(`/`config.replace(` outside the gate.

verdict.reasoning: Every cited line verified. concepts.ts:447-452 exposes get() (no reason/key) and replace(next, reason) on the adapter contract; the OpenClaw impl (packages/adapter-openclaw/src/runtime.ts:1033-1064) returns the entire provider config from get() with no audit — strictly broader than the raw('*') read that runtime-config-raw.ts:19-73 allowlists only for onboarding and audits via appendAudit. Consumers verified leaking OpenClaw schema outside the adapter: plugins/models/index.ts:33-54 (RuntimeModelConfig mirrors agents.defaults.model.primary / agents.list[].subagents.model) with whole-config get→mutate→replace at 83-99; plugins/team/index.ts:216-219; src/core/openclaw-integration.ts:41-71 (rewrites mcp.servers, replaces full config). The arch test (tests/architecture/adapter-boundary.test.ts:79-82) denies only config.raw/.raw<, so all of this passes. The lost-update hazard from full-file replace() is mechanically real, and an extra verified wrinkle strengthens it: get() synthesizes agents.list (runtime.ts:1041), which the models plugin's replace() then materializes back into the provider file. The project's own doc (.claude/knowledge/adapter-architecture.md:91-114) prescribes typed adapter methods or the audited allowlist for provider-shaped access, so this is a genuine governance bypass, not intentional design. Minor nit: the recommendation to make update() deep-merge is already implemented (runtime.ts:1043-1046) — the issue is consumers use replace() instead. No concrete immediate damage on a single-user system, so P1 (refactor-effort fix), not P0.

confirmed.title: Core statically depends on workflows-plugin internals — plugin registries acting as core infrastructure
confirmed.evidence: src/lib/plugin-registry.ts:29-35 imports registerPluginDefinition from plugins/workflows/lib/source-registry, registerPluginNodeType/unregisterPluginNodeTypes from plugins/workflows/lib/node-type-registry, and the notification-channel-registry — and calls them in the generic plugin lifecycle (lines 642-646, 862, 872), so the CORE plugin loader cannot function without the workflows plugin's source tree. src/core/plugin-host/reload-pipeline.ts:40-41 and src/core/agent-packages/post-sync-reload.ts:13 (clearSkillCache from plugins/workflows/lib/skill-loader) repeat the pattern. scripts/lib/post-channel.ts:13 (a core MCP exec tool) imports resolveFile from @bakin/assets/lib/asset-service even though assets registers an assets.resolveServe hook (plugins/assets/index.ts:416). This directly contradicts CLAUDE.md's 'Cross-plugin and core ↔ plugin calls go exclusively through the HookRegistry' — while .claude/knowledge/repo-architecture.md's alias table sanctions @bakin/{plugin} for 'App + test code', so the two documents conflict. Net effect: workflows is not a plugin, it's load-bearing core, and the 'plugins are independently activatable modules' story is false for it.
confirmed.recommendation: Move the cross-cutting registries (workflow source-registry, node-type-registry, notification-channel-registry, skill cache) into packages/core/src — they are extension points the plugin loader owns, exactly like hook-registry already is. Have the workflows plugin consume them via ctx like everyone else. Convert post-channel's resolveFile call to the assets.resolveServe hook. Then reconcile CLAUDE.md vs repo-architecture.md on whether app code may ever import plugin internals.

verdict.reasoning: Every cited line verified by reading the files. src/lib/plugin-registry.ts:29-35 imports the workflows plugin's source-registry, node-type-registry, and notification-channel-registry via relative paths into plugins/workflows/lib/, and the GENERIC plugin lifecycle depends on them: the deactivate sweep calls unregisterPluginNodeTypes/unregisterPluginNotificationChannels at lines 642-646, and the PluginContext handed to every plugin delegates registerWorkflow to registerPluginDefinition (line 862) and registerNodeType to registerPluginNodeType (line 872). src/core/plugin-host/reload-pipeline.ts:40-41 and src/core/agent-packages/post-sync-reload.ts:13 (clearSkillCache, called line 28) repeat the pattern. scripts/lib/post-channel.ts:13 imports resolveFile from @bakin/assets/lib/asset-service (used line 37) while plugins/assets/index.ts registers assets.resolveServe and assets.saveFromSource hooks whose own comments call hooks 'the sanctioned way for core'. The doc conflict is also real: CLAUDE.md says core-plugin calls go 'exclusively through the HookRegistry' while .claude/knowledge/repo-architecture.md:244 sanctions @bakin/<id> for 'App + test code (never cross-plugin)'. No architecture test enforces the hook-only rule (tests/architecture/ has only adapter-boundary and embedded-assets tests), so drift is unguarded. The finding's core claim — workflows is load-bearing core masquerading as a plugin — is accurate. Not P0: all core plugins are statically compiled into the binary (plugin-static-imports.ts), so no runtime failure mode exists today; this is structural debt with a clear, bounded fix (move the registries into packages/core like hook-registry, use the existing assets hook in post-channel, reconcile the two docs). P1 confirmed.

confirmed.title: Six dead files (~620 LOC) unreachable from any import surface
confirmed.evidence: Verified by extracting every import/require/dynamic-import specifier in the repo (6,853 unique) and then re-grepping each candidate's path stem AND every named export across src/, packages/, plugins/, cli/, scripts/, tests/, dev/, server.ts, .github/, and docs/. (1) plugins/tasks/components/new-task-dialog.tsx (227 lines, exports NewTaskDialog at line 28): zero code references; the only hits are a docs screenshot ID (scripts/docs/screenshot-manifest.yaml:69) and an tag (docs/src/content/docs/using/tasks.md:26) — the live new-task UI is implemented in kanban-board.tsx/task-detail-dialog.tsx, which do not import it. (2) plugins/team/components/curated-browser.tsx (167 lines, exports CuratedBrowser at line 44): zero references to the file or symbol anywhere in code; only mention is .claude/knowledge/agent-packages.md. (3) src/components/calendar/calendar-view.tsx (104 lines, exports CalendarView at line 16): zero references; its sole dependency consumer relationship makes (4) src/lib/parsers/calendar.ts (46 lines, parseCalendar at line 3) dead too — calendar-view.tsx:4 is parseCalendar's only importer. (5) src/components/plugin-slot.tsx (32 lines, PluginSlot at line 13): zero importers; packages/sdk/src/components/index.ts:74-76 explicitly documents 'PluginSlot is NOT re-exported here... pulls in server-only plugin-registry state and breaks'. (6) src/core/cli/ui/panel.tsx (17 lines, Panel at line 9): zero importers — grep for any '...panel'-suffixed specifier across the repo returns nothing; the Ink TUI in src/core/cli/ui/readonly.tsx does not use it. (7) packages/host/src/components/layout/skeleton-loader.tsx (28 lines, PageSkeleton line 5 / WithLoading line 24): neither symbol nor the file stem is referenced anywhere. Counter-example proving the method catches indirect consumers: src/cli/schedule.ts initially looked dead but is ALIVE via cli/bakin.ts:19 — it was excluded from this finding.
confirmed.recommendation: Delete all seven files. For new-task-dialog.tsx, the docs screenshot pipeline captures the live UI by route, not by component file, so deletion is safe. Re-run bun run test + bun run typecheck + bun run build:plugins after deletion to confirm.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every claim by reading/grepping the cited files. All seven files are dead: (1) new-task-dialog.tsx — zero code importers; the live new-task UI is TaskDetailDrawer wired in kanban-board.tsx:11,445-448, and the screenshot pipeline (scripts/docs/screenshot-manifest.yaml:69-80) drives the running app by route + button click, never by component import, so deletion is safe. (2) curated-browser.tsx CuratedBrowser (line 44) — zero references. (3) calendar-view.tsx CalendarView (line 16) — zero importers. (4) parsers/calendar.ts parseCalendar (line 3) — sole importer is the dead calendar-view.tsx:4. (5) plugin-slot.tsx — zero importers; packages/sdk/src/components/index.ts:74-76 documents it is deliberately not re-exported. (6) src/core/cli/ui/panel.tsx Panel — zero importers; the only other Panel in the repo is @xyflow/react's Panel in workflow-canvas-editor.tsx:26 (verified import block); no file under src/core/cli besides panel.tsx contains 'panel'. (7) skeleton-loader.tsx PageSkeleton/WithLoading — self-references only, no barrel in the layout dir. Checked indirect vectors: no template-string dynamic imports anywhere, no test/.github/docs-source code references, build entries tree-walk from imports. P1 is appropriate: zero runtime damage, but this is exactly the tech-debt-reduction work the refactor effort targets, and the stale NewTaskDialog (a convincing-looking parallel implementation of the live dialog) is a real confusion hazard for future edits. Minor nit: the title says six files but the finding correctly lists and proves seven.

confirmed.title: Runtime circular-dependency cluster centered on plugin-registry ↔ scripts/lib/registry ↔ task-service ↔ dispatch (17 cycles)
confirmed.evidence: madge --circular over server.ts + src + packages/core/src + packages/sdk/src + cli (533 files) reports 17 circular dependencies; 14 of them route through one cluster. Key runtime (non-type) edges personally verified: src/lib/plugin-registry.ts:46 imports addExecTool/removeExecToolsByPlugin from scripts/lib/registry; scripts/lib/registry.ts:11 imports getHookRegistry back from src/lib/plugin-registry (both value imports — a hard runtime cycle); scripts/lib/registry.ts:21-24 imports src/lib/plugin-context-services, whose line 71 lazy-imports src/core/task-service; task-service.ts:15 imports continuation, continuation.ts:15 imports dispatch, and dispatch.ts:15+27 import plugin-registry and task-store, closing the loop. The codebase already papers over this with dynamic imports and apology comments: src/core/task-store.ts:200 ('await import(../lib/plugin-registry)'), src/core/app-services.ts:19 ('await import(./task-store)'), scripts/lib/registry.ts:100 ('safe against the plugin-registry ↔ registry circular by...'), src/lib/plugin-registry.ts:265 ('module can't import plugin-registry directly (circular)'), packages/core/src/plugins/lockfile.ts:265 ('avoid a circular dependency'). Compounding it, the exec-tool registry — a core runtime module that builds full PluginContext objects and is imported by src/core/mcp-server.ts, src/core/bakin-skill.ts, src/core/plugin-host/reload-pipeline.ts, and packages/host/src/api/exec-tools/[toolName].ts — lives under scripts/lib/, a directory CLAUDE.md describes as 'build infrastructure'.
confirmed.recommendation: Two-step refactor: (1) move scripts/lib/registry.ts into src/core/ (e.g. src/core/exec-tool-registry.ts) since it is runtime code, not build tooling; (2) break the hub by extracting the PluginContext factory out of the registry module and extracting the pure registry maps (exec tools, hooks) into leaf modules with no src/core imports, so plugin-registry, task-service, and dispatch all depend downward on leaves instead of on each other. The existing globalThis-backed state makes the extraction mechanical.

verdict.reasoning: Finding fully verified by independent reproduction and file reads. (1) Madge over the same 533-file scope reports exactly 17 circular dependencies; cycles 4-17 all route through the plugin-registry/scripts-lib-registry cluster as claimed. (2) The hard runtime cycle is real: src/lib/plugin-registry.ts:46 value-imports addExecTool/removeExecToolsByPlugin from scripts/lib/registry, and scripts/lib/registry.ts:11 value-imports getHookRegistry back from src/lib/plugin-registry; registry.ts:100-102 contains a comment explicitly acknowledging the cycle is only safe due to evaluation timing. (3) The longer loop is verified edge by edge: registry.ts:19-23 imports plugin-context-services; plugin-context-services.ts:71 dynamic-imports src/core/task-service; task-service.ts:15 imports continuation; continuation.ts:15 imports dispatch; dispatch.ts:15 imports plugin-registry and lines 21-27 import task-store. (4) All four cited apology comments exist at the cited lines (task-store.ts:200, app-services.ts:19, plugin-registry.ts:264-266, lockfile.ts:262-266). (5) The mislocation claim holds: scripts/lib/registry.ts is imported at runtime by src/core/mcp-server.ts:34, src/core/bakin-skill.ts:45, src/core/plugin-host/reload-pipeline.ts:39, and packages/host/src/api/exec-tools/[toolName].ts:9, while CLAUDE.md describes scripts/ as build infrastructure. Severity: P1, not P0 — no runtime breakage is demonstrable today (dynamic imports defuse the cycles at load time), but this is genuine hub-of-the-system coupling debt with accumulating workarounds and documented mock-fragility costs (the user's own memory notes partial task-store mocks break whenever new imports land in this cluster), and the proposed extraction is mechanical thanks to the globalThis-backed registry state. Fits squarely in 'fix in this refactor effort'.

confirmed.title: Core plugin loader hard-imports workflows plugin internals, violating the documented HookRegistry-only boundary
confirmed.evidence: CLAUDE.md states 'Cross-plugin and core ↔ plugin calls go exclusively through the HookRegistry'. But src/lib/plugin-registry.ts — the core module that loads all plugins — statically imports one specific plugin's internals: line 29 registerPluginDefinition from '../../plugins/workflows/lib/source-registry', line 30 type WorkflowDefinition from '../../plugins/workflows/types', line 31 registerPluginNodeType/unregisterPluginNodeTypes from '../../plugins/workflows/lib/node-type-registry', lines 32-35 registerPluginNotificationChannel/unregisterPluginNotificationChannels from '../../plugins/workflows/lib/notification-channel-registry'. This is the only core→plugin internal import outside the documented/intentional plugin-static-imports.ts (#421) and the SDK re-export surface. It also drags plugins/workflows code into every consumer of plugin-registry (which includes cli-adjacent and test code) and is the entry edge for madge cycle #4 (plugin-registry > source-registry > workflows/types > workflow-skill-drift — though that inner edge is import-type only).
confirmed.recommendation: Move the three registries (workflow source, node-type, notification-channel) into core (they are core extension points that plugins feed, not workflows-plugin features), or have the workflows plugin register them via the HookRegistry during activate() like every other cross-boundary call. Then plugin-registry only knows generic registration interfaces.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading every cited file. src/lib/plugin-registry.ts:29-35 statically imports plugin-internal modules from plugins/workflows (source-registry, types, node-type-registry, notification-channel-registry), used at lines 642-647 and 859-895. CLAUDE.md documents HookRegistry as the exclusive core-to-plugin channel, and no architecture test or knowledge doc exempts this edge (tests/architecture/ enforces only the adapter boundary and embedded assets). The asymmetry is demonstrable in the same file: lines 36-39 import the health-check registry from src/core (../core/health-check-registry) — core already hosts that registry in core for the identical extension-point role, so the recommended fix follows existing precedent. The cycle claim verified: workflow-skill-drift.ts:7 value-imports getPluginSkills from src/lib/plugin-registry while plugin-registry reaches source-registry, which pulls workflows/types, whose edge to workflow-skill-drift is type-only (as the finding disclosed). Coupling impact is real: node-type-registry imports zod and self-registers builtin node types at module load, so every consumer of plugin-registry (which exports the ubiquitous getHookRegistry) drags workflows plugin code. One inaccuracy: the claim this is the only core-to-plugin internal import is false — src/core/agent-packages/load-sources.ts:44,49, package-integrity.ts:5-6, post-sync-reload.ts:13, and src/core/plugin-host/reload-pipeline.ts:40-41 also import workflows internals. That widens the violation rather than refuting it, though it means the proposed registry relocation only partially closes the breach (parser/skill-loader imports remain). confirmed.title: Two entry points with circular delegation glued together by monkey-patching process.exit and process.argv
confirmed.evidence: src/core/cli.ts:240-262 delegateToSourceCli replaces process.argv and process.exit (lines 243-247) with a version that throws DelegatedCliExit, then dynamic-imports cli/bakin.ts's main(). In the other direction, cli/bakin.ts:2698-2704 (cmdStartServer) imports dispatchCli from src/core/cli.ts for the onboarding gate, and cli/bakin.ts:4458 (case 'dev') imports cmdDev from src/core/cli.ts — a mutual dependency between the two entrypoints. The seam leaks: cli/bakin.ts:4588 must special-case re-throwing errors named 'BakinDelegatedCliExit' inside its own catch, and 4591 special-cases a second exit-as-exception convention (/^exit:\d+$/). cli/bakin.ts uses process.exit liberally (e.g. exitCommandIssue at 305, exitCommandFailure at 350, main's catch at 4622), so every one of those becomes a thrown exception when invoked through the binary — any broad catch added inside a command handler would silently swallow the exit code. src/core/cli.ts:309-312 also has explicit 'status'/'stop'/'plugins' cases that are byte-identical to the default case at 314-318.
confirmed.recommendation: Collapse to one dispatcher. server.ts should call a single runCli(argv) in src/core/cli/ that returns {startServer, exitCode}; cli/bakin.ts becomes a 3-line shim for the package.json bin entry (package.json:10 points 'bakin' at ./cli/bakin.ts). Commands return exit codes instead of calling process.exit, eliminating DelegatedCliExit, the argv/exit monkey-patch, and both exit-as-exception conventions.

verdict.reasoning:
Every cited line verified by direct reading; the finding survives attack.

(1) Monkey-patching confirmed: src/core/cli.ts:240-262 `delegateToSourceCli` replaces process.argv (line 243) and process.exit (244-247) with a thrower of `DelegatedCliExit`, then dynamic-imports cli/bakin.ts's main() (line 250). Globals are restored in finally, but during delegation ANY process.exit call anywhere in the process throws instead of exiting, and process.argv is globally mutated.

(2) Mutual dependency confirmed: cli/bakin.ts:2697-2704 (`cmdStartServer`) imports `dispatchCli` from ../src/core/cli for the start gate, and cli/bakin.ts:4458 (case 'dev') imports `cmdDev` from the same module — while src/core/cli.ts:250 imports cli/bakin.ts's main. It is mutual import, not an actual infinite loop ('start' short-circuits in dispatchCli at lines 284-288 without delegating back), but the bidirectional coupling is real. server.ts:93/113 confirms dispatchCli is the binary entry; cli/bakin.ts:4630-4631 (`import.meta.main`) confirms the dual-entry arrangement.

(3) Seam leakage confirmed and slightly worse than claimed: cli/bakin.ts:4588-4590 re-throws errors matched by NAME STRING 'BakinDelegatedCliExit' (instanceof is impossible across the two module instances — inherently fragile). cli/bakin.ts:4591-4593 special-cases a SECOND exit-as-exception convention /^exit:\d+$/ which I traced to test mocks only (tests/cli/readonly-commands.test.ts:49,67; tests/cli/system-actions.test.ts:70 throw `Error('exit:${code}')` from mocked process.exit) — test-harness convention baked into production catch logic.

(4) Swallow hazard confirmed: cli/bakin.ts has 59 `process.exit` call sites; exitCommandIssue (line 305) and exitCommandFailure (line 350) both call process.exit(1) followed by `throw new Error('unreachable')`. Under the binary, line-305/350 exits become thrown DelegatedCliExit; any future broad try/catch inside a command handler would intercept it, and delegateToSourceCli would then return exitCode 0 (src/core/cli.ts:252) — a failing command silently reporting success, but only in the compiled-binary path, making it hard to catch in dev.

(5) Dead duplication confirmed: src/core/cli.ts:309-312 ('status'/'stop'/'plugins') and the default case at 314-319 both execute `return await delegateToSourceCli(argv)` — behaviorally identical, differing only in comments.

Severity: P1 is correct. No concrete immediate damage on this single-user system (the mechanism currently works, exit codes do propagate), so P0 is not warranted. But it is a latent correctness trap (silent exit-code swallowing, global mutation during async delegation, string-name error matching, test conventions in prod control flow) squarely in the cli-consolidation dimension of this tech-debt refactor — exactly 'fix in this refactor effort'. The recommended collapse to one dispatcher returning exit codes is sound; package.json bin and import.meta.main guard confirm cli/bakin.ts can become a thin shim.

confirmed.title: Behavioral disagreements between the binary dispatcher and the source CLI: no-arg behavior differs, and `bakin update` is advertised but unimplemented in the npm-bin entry
confirmed.evidence: (1) No-arg: compiled binary treats no arguments as `start` (src/core/cli.ts:277-278, `const cmd = args[0] ?? 'start'`), while the package.json-bin entry cli/bakin.ts:4099-4103 prints help and exits 0 on no arguments; the unused canonical parser (src/core/cli/parser.ts:80-90) sides with the binary ('start'). (3) Duplicate version implementations confirmed at src/core/cli.ts:296-299 and cli/bakin.ts:4110-4115; currently consistent but drift-prone. confirmed.title: Consolidation target: src/core/cli/ as the single CLI package with one file per command group; cli/bakin.ts shrinks to a bin shim
confirmed.evidence: Verified inventory: src/core/cli.ts (330 lines) owns start/serve gate + version/update/dev/help and delegates everything else (309-318); cli/bakin.ts (4,632 lines) owns status, dispatch, tasks (8 subs, 4125-4163), workflows (4), agents incl. agent-packages + lessons (10, 4182-4231), settings (3), diagnostics, plugins (11 subs incl. publish/scaffold/link, 4256-4370), packages (4), stop, logs, setup service, paths, mkdir, check (9), install (7), onboard, doctor + fix/delegate/repair (~630 lines, 1890-2520), reboot/restart, reindex, docs, search, search:stats, trash, schedule (handlers in src/cli/schedule.ts, 237 lines), plus dynamic plugin commands (3761-3787). confirmed.title: Agent avatar endpoint joins request-controlled `id` into a filesystem path with no containment check
confirmed.evidence: `agents/avatar.ts:12` reads `id = url.searchParams.get('id')`, then `:18` builds `avatarPath = join(agents, id, 'avatar.jpg')` and `:24` reads/returns it. There is NO regex/normalization/containment check on `id` (compare the rest of the codebase: `isValidAssetId` in plugins/assets/lib/asset-id.ts, `PLUGIN_ID_RE`, and the `relPath.includes('..')` guard in plugins/assets.ts:45). `server.ts:548` dispatches `GET /api/agents/avatar` straight to this handler, so any tailnet device can request `?id=../../../../some/dir` and the server resolves `join(~/.bakin/agents, '../../../../some/dir', 'avatar.jpg')`, escaping the agents directory. Unlike the memory workspace route (api/plugins/memory/workspace.ts:27 gates on `runtime.agents.get(agentId)` before any path use), this handler never validates that `id` is a real agent. Exploit is bounded by the fixed trailing `avatar.jpg` segment (an attacker can only read files literally named `avatar.jpg` outside the store and probe directory existence via 200-vs-404), so confidentiality impact is limited, but it is a confirmed missing-containment traversal.
confirmed.recommendation: Validate `id` against the same agent-id shape used elsewhere (e.g. `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$/` or reject any `id` containing `/`, `\`, or `..`) before the `join`, and/or realpath-contain the resolved `avatarPath` to `getBakinPaths().agents` (resolved + `startsWith(root + sep)`). Return 400 on rejection.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every claim by reading the files. packages/host/src/api/agents/avatar.ts:12 takes `id` from the query string, :18 joins it into a path under ~/.bakin/agents with zero validation (only a falsy check at :13), and :24 readFileSync's the result. server.ts:548-551 dispatches GET /api/agents/avatar straight to this handler via dispatchWebHandler, which (verified in packages/host/src/api/_adapter.ts:35-67) performs no sanitization — it just builds `new URL(req.url)` and forwards. No global traversal guard exists in server.ts ahead of the route (grepped). searchParams.get percent-decodes, so `?id=../../../..` escapes the agents directory; unlike the memory workspace route, there is no agent-existence gate. Exploit impact is bounded by the fixed trailing `avatar.jpg` segment (can only read files literally named avatar.jpg outside the store, plus a directory-existence oracle via 200-vs-404), and the trust perimeter is a single-user tailnet — so no demonstrable concrete damage warranting P0. But it is a confirmed missing-containment traversal in a codebase that validates equivalent inputs elsewhere, reachable by any tailnet device or any agent making HTTP calls, with a one-line fix. P1: fix in this refactor.

confirmed.title: Shell command injection in legacy plugin installer (dead code, but live test keeps it re-adoptable)
confirmed.evidence: src/core/plugin-installer.ts:116 builds a shell string from user-controlled input: `execSync(`git clone --depth 1 ${gitUrl} ${tempDir}`, { stdio: 'pipe' })`. `gitUrl` (line 112) is taken verbatim from the caller's `repo` argument when it starts with `http` (e.g. `https://github.com/x/y.git; rm -rf ~`), or `https://github.com/${repo.replace(/^github:/,'')}.git` otherwise — no shell-metacharacter validation. This is a textbook OS-command-injection in a shell context. I confirmed it is currently unreachable from production: grepping src/packages/cli/plugins/scripts for `installFromGithub`/`installFromPath`/`plugin-installer` returns only the function definitions, the internal `installFromGithub`->`installFromPath` call, and `tests/core/plugin-installer.test.ts`. The live CLI path (`cli/bakin.ts:1120 cmdPluginsInstall` -> `apiPost('/api/plugins/install')`) routes to the hardened `packages/host/src/api/plugins/install.ts`, which never imports this module. So this is a pre-#147 dead installer — but it still ships, still compiles, and `tests/core/plugin-installer.test.ts:21` exercises both functions, which is exactly the condition under which a future contributor wires it back into a route and reintroduces instant RCE.
confirmed.recommendation: Delete src/core/plugin-installer.ts and its test. The production installer (packages/host/src/api/plugins/install.ts + src/core/github-source-cache.ts) already covers github/local installs with argv-array git invocation, ref validation, and path containment; this legacy file is pure liability. verdict.reasoning:

confirmed.title: @makinbakin/sdk/types is a hand-maintained fork of packages/core/src/plugin-types.ts with no parity enforcement — and in-repo plugins bypass it entirely
confirmed.evidence: The plugin contract types are declared twice as independent text: HealthCheckResult at packages/core/src/plugin-types.ts:306-311 and again at packages/sdk/src/types/index.ts:1079-1088; the same is true for HealthRepairSafety/Change/PlanItem/ApplyResult/Handler and PluginHealthCheckInput (core:313-358 vs sdk:1090-1135), ExecToolDefinition (sdk:999), PluginContext (core:377-442 vs sdk:1205+), and BakinPlugin (sdk:1253). packages/sdk/src/types/index.ts imports nothing from core (only react and zod types at lines 9-10). 17 plugin server files import the CORE copy via relative paths — e.g. plugins/schedule/lib/health-checks.ts:16, plugins/tasks/lib/health-checks.ts:16, plugins/memory/lib/health-checks.ts:17, plugins/health/lib/system-checks/sync-skill.ts:12 — grep counts 12x '../../../../packages/core/src/plugin-types' + 5x '../../../packages/core/src/plugin-types'. CLAUDE.md states 'The single canonical result type is HealthCheckResult from @makinbakin/sdk', yet zero plugin health-check files import it from the SDK. tests/sdk/ contains only lazy.test.tsx, register.test.ts, slots.test.tsx — no type-parity test, so the published SDK copy can silently drift from what the server actually enforces (it already has for AvailableModel, see separate finding).
confirmed.recommendation: Pick one source of truth. Simplest: have packages/core/src/plugin-types.ts re-export the contract types from packages/sdk/src/types (the SDK has zero deps so the dependency direction is safe in-workspace; the publish pipeline already bundles SDK source standalone via scripts/build-sdk-package.ts). Then migrate the 17 plugin import sites to `import type { HealthCheckResult, HealthRepairHandler } from '@makinbakin/sdk'` — the root barrel is server-safe per plugin-system.md. If a re-export is not feasible, add a tsc-level parity test (e.g. `const _check: SdkHealthCheckResult satisfies CoreHealthCheckResult` pairs in tests/sdk/type-parity.test.ts). Type-only — zero vendor-bundle weight.

verdict.reasoning: Every cited line verified. HealthCheckResult duplicated verbatim (packages/core/src/plugin-types.ts:306-311 vs packages/sdk/src/types/index.ts:1079-1088); same for the HealthRepair* family and PluginHealthCheckInput (core:313-370 vs sdk:1090-1134), PluginContext (core:377-442 vs sdk:1205-1250), ExecToolDefinition (sdk:999), BakinPlugin (sdk:1253). SDK types file imports only react+zod (lines 9-10) and declares itself intentionally self-contained; nothing generates or checks parity (tests/sdk/ has only lazy/register/slots tests; build-sdk-package.ts builds from the standalone source). 19 plugin import lines pull the CORE copy via relative paths (e.g. plugins/schedule/lib/health-checks.ts:16, plugins/tasks/lib/health-checks.ts:16, plugins/memory/lib/health-checks.ts:17, 12 files in plugins/health/lib/system-checks/), and zero import HealthCheckResult from @makinbakin/sdk despite CLAUDE.md naming the SDK export canonical. Drift is already demonstrable: SDK AvailableModel (sdk:1329, name?/provider?/tier? optional, has source?) diverges from the server's plugins/models/types.ts:20 (name/tier/provider required, has providerBrandColor?), and core's @deprecated JSDoc on registerRoute is absent from the SDK copy. The only refutation angle — duplication is deliberate for a dependency-free published package — does not survive: deliberate duplication with no parity enforcement and demonstrated drift is exactly the claimed tech debt. Not P0 (type-only, no runtime damage, health-check types currently in sync); P1 is right for a published-SDK contract drifting from server enforcement, cheap to fix in this refactor.

confirmed.title: AvailableModel is declared twice and has already drifted; three call sites hand-fetch /api/plugins/models/available with no SDK data hook behind ModelSelect

confirmed.title: No SDK primitive for subscribing to plugin SSE events — host content store hardcodes per-plugin bump counters, and the assets plugin opens three parallel EventSource connections as a workaround
confirmed.evidence: The shell owns one singleton SSE connection (src/hooks/use-sse.ts) but its event routing is hardcoded to specific plugins: `data.type === 'taskboard'` → bumpTaskboard (use-sse.ts:57), plus doctor and reindex handling; the host content store carries plugin-specific state fields taskboardVersion/doctorVersion/reindexProgress (src/hooks/use-content-store.ts:22-25) and bumpTaskboard/bumpDoctor actions (lines 72-73). Tasks and health plugins consume these via useContentStore (plugins/tasks/components/kanban-board.tsx:136, plugins/tasks/hooks/use-task-summary.ts:23, plugins/health/hooks/use-health-summary.ts:23, plugins/health/components/health-page.tsx:473-474). The assets plugin got no such carve-out, so it opens its OWN EventSource('/api/events') in three separate components — plugins/assets/components/task-assets.tsx:33, versioned/VersionedAssetGrid.tsx:244, versioned/VersionedAssetDetail.tsx:41 — each parsing raw `plugin-event` payloads ('asset.changed'/'asset.removed'); VersionedAssetDetail also resorts to a window CustomEvent bus ('bakin:asset-uploaded', line ~260). The SDK has no client event surface at all (grep for EventSource/plugin-event/addEventListener across packages/sdk/src/ returns nothing). Every extra EventSource is an extra held-open HTTP connection per mounted component, and an external plugin author has no sanctioned way to react to their own broadcast() events.
confirmed.recommendation: Add `usePluginEvent(eventName, handler)` (or `useSSEEvent`) to @makinbakin/sdk/hooks that multiplexes the existing singleton connection — implement as a listener registry the host use-sse.ts forwards `plugin-event` messages into. Migrate assets' three raw EventSources, then replace the hardcoded taskboardVersion/doctorVersion/reindexProgress fields with the same primitive so the host store stops knowing about individual plugins. Weight: negligible — a Map of listeners in the existing sdk-hooks bundle.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading every cited file. (1) Shell SSE singleton hardcodes per-plugin routing: src/hooks/use-sse.ts:57-58 routes data.type==='taskboard' to bumpTaskboard, line 92 routes audit event 'doctor.run' to bumpDoctor, lines 155-163 route reindex.* to setReindexProgress, and lines 108-137 special-case workflow.* plugin-events. (2) Host store carries plugin-specific fields: src/hooks/use-content-store.ts:22-25 (taskboardVersion/doctorVersion/reindexProgress) and 72-73 (bumpTaskboard/bumpDoctor). (3) Tasks/health plugins consume these via useContentStore re-exported at packages/sdk/src/hooks/index.ts:13 — confirmed at plugins/tasks/components/kanban-board.tsx:136, plugins/tasks/hooks/use-task-summary.ts:23, plugins/health/hooks/use-health-summary.ts:23, plugins/health/components/health-page.tsx:473-474. (4) Assets plugin opens three separate EventSource('/api/events') connections: task-assets.tsx:33, VersionedAssetGrid.tsx:244, VersionedAssetDetail.tsx:41, each hand-parsing 'plugin-event' payloads for asset.changed/asset.removed — extra held-open HTTP connections per mounted component on an HTTP/1.1 origin with a ~6-connection browser cap. (5) No generic client event primitive exists anywhere: grep for usePluginEvent/useSSEEvent/pluginEvent across packages/ and src/ returns nothing; packages/sdk/src has zero EventSource/plugin-event matches; the exported useSSE takes no event name or handler. One evidence error: the 'bakin:asset-uploaded' CustomEvent bus is misattributed to VersionedAssetDetail — the listener is actually in task-assets.tsx:52 and the dispatcher in VersionedAssetGrid.tsx:275 — but the workaround exists in the assets plugin as claimed, so this does not undermine the finding. Severity P1 is correct: no active damage (not P0), but a genuine SDK gap with three in-repo workaround sites, host-store coupling to individual plugins (contrary to the codebase's registry-based plugin-communication pattern), and a cheap, well-scoped fix that fits the current refactor effort.

confirmed.title: Externals contract still duplicated in two build entry points despite externals.ts being the declared single source of truth
confirmed.evidence: src/core/whiskit/externals.ts's docblock says the externals list 'was previously duplicated in user-plugin-builder.ts and scripts/build-plugins.ts — if one added an SDK sub-path the other didn't, plugins broke inconsistently' and exports PLUGIN_CLIENT_EXTERNALS as the single source. scripts/build-plugins.ts:17,26 correctly imports it. All three are content-identical today, but a new SDK subpath added only to externals.ts would be silently inlined into the production shell bundle (second SDK instance, breaking the one-React/one-SDK import-map invariant) and into dev plugin hot-swap bundles.
confirmed.recommendation: Import PLUGIN_CLIENT_EXTERNALS from src/core/whiskit/externals.ts in both packages/host/build.ts and scripts/dev.ts, deleting the inline arrays. Consider adding an architecture test that greps build entry points for hardcoded '@makinbakin/sdk/' externals.

verdict.reasoning: Every cited line checks out. src/core/whiskit/externals.ts:1-12,41 declares itself the single source of truth for PLUGIN_CLIENT_EXTERNALS (15 specifiers) and its docblock documents that this exact duplication previously caused inconsistent plugin breakage. scripts/build-plugins.ts:17,26 and src/core/whiskit/build.ts:28 (the user-plugin path) correctly consume it. But packages/host/build.ts:37-53 hardcodes an entry-identical 15-specifier copy and is the release-path shell build (package.json:19 build:host-shell, chained in build at package.json:15, run in .github/workflows/release.yml:159). scripts/dev.ts:77-85 hardcodes a third identical copy (EXTERNAL), actually used at dev.ts:335 via buildOnePlugin, whose --external flags (scripts/dev-build-one-plugin.ts:66,75-76,92) drive HMR plugin rebuilds. The claimed failure mode is real: an SDK sub-path added only to externals.ts would be silently inlined into the production shell bundle and dev hot-swap bundles, creating a second SDK module instance and breaking the one-React/one-SDK import-map invariant — the documented historical bug class. Nothing prevents both files from importing the pure-constants module. Not P0 (lists identical today, no current damage), but P1 fits a tech-debt-focused refactor: trivial fix, prevents a recurrence of a bug the codebase already shipped once.

confirmed.title: scripts/docs/check.ts copy-pastes ~150 lines of renderers from generate.ts and the copies have already diverged
confirmed.evidence: check.ts duplicates from generate.ts: commandSnippets (check.ts:116 vs generate.ts:56), renderCommandSnippet (check.ts:123 vs generate.ts:102), renderApiRoutesSnippet (check.ts:182 vs generate.ts:139), escapeTableCell (check.ts:197 vs generate.ts:154), renderSettingsSnippet (check.ts:201 vs generate.ts:158), renderPluginPermissionsSnippet (check.ts:224 vs generate.ts:181), and docsSnippetBlocks (check.ts:21 vs generate.ts:71). verdict.reasoning: Verified every citation by reading both files. check.ts duplicates ~150 lines from generate.ts: commandSnippets (check.ts:116-121 == generate.ts:56-61), docsSnippetBlocks (check.ts:21-38 == generate.ts:71-88), renderCommandSnippet (check.ts:123-158 vs generate.ts:102-137), renderApiRoutesSnippet (check.ts:182-195 vs generate.ts:139-152), escapeTableCell (check.ts:197-199 == generate.ts:154-156), renderSettingsSnippet (check.ts:201-222 vs generate.ts:158-179), renderPluginPermissionsSnippet (check.ts:224-239 == generate.ts:181-196), plus renderDocsSnippetBlock (check.ts:325-338 vs generate.ts:198-213) which the finding did not even count. Divergence confirmed by diff: generate.ts throws on unknown marker/missing command/empty settings/empty routes (generate.ts:120,131,141,160) while check.ts returns '' (check.ts:141,152,184,203). The validators (check.ts:166-180, 241-295) re-render with check.ts's own copies and string-compare against file content, so the rendered output contract must be edited in lockstep across both files. CI gate confirmed: ci-pr.yml:51, ci-main.yml:48, docs-deploy.yml:55 all run `bun run docs:check`, which package.json:43 defines as docs:generate then docs:validate (check.ts). One nuance: because docs:check regenerates before validating, the 'stale generated blocks pass' scenario is largely mitigated for the deploy path; the real exposure is (a) any output-format edit to one copy but not the other fails CI with a misleading 'out of sync' error immediately after a successful generate, and (b) the divergent return-'' semantics produce a misleading 'out of sync' message for a genuinely missing CLI command (check.ts:152 -> :177), and CI lacks a git-diff check so committed docs can drift silently. The core claim — congruent copy-pasted render contract validated by string equality in a CI gate, with drift already present — is fully verified. No data damage possible, so not P0; as an active lockstep maintenance trap in a tech-debt-focused refactor, P1 stands.

deferred.title: Published SDK source reaches outside its package into src/ and two plugins (inverted dependency, package-level cycle)
deferred.evidence: The npm-published @makinbakin/sdk package's source re-exports from repo-internal aliases that resolve outside packages/sdk: packages/sdk/src/ui/index.ts:10+ re-exports every component from '@/components/ui/*' (repo-root src/components/ui — the 'Next.js-era tree' acknowledged as misplaced in packages/host/src/routes/settings.tsx:11-14); packages/sdk/src/hooks/index.ts:53-69 re-exports nine hooks from '@bakin/team/hooks/use-agent-store' and :74-78 from '@bakin/workflows/hooks/use-notification-channels'; packages/sdk/src/components/index.ts:88 re-exports ChannelIcon from '@bakin/workflows/hooks/channel-icon'.
