deferred.title: cli/bakin.ts is a 4,632-line god-file that mixes HTTP-client commands with direct server-internal imports
deferred.evidence: cli/bakin.ts is 4,632 lines — the largest file in the repo (next largest is 2,808). Despite CLAUDE.md describing it as 'the HTTP-client CLI', it imports server-side internals directly: line 8 assemblePluginArtifact/indexFromEntries from src/core/whiskit/publish, line 20 getSettings/updateSettings from src/core/settings (direct ~/.bakin/settings.json mutation from a separate process while the server may hold its own settings state), line 7 APP_VERSION from packages/core/src/constants. It owns ~20 command families (doctor, dispatch, tasks, agents, packages, schedule, search, trash, settings, logs, paths, reindex, restart, docs, onboard, init, mkdir, check, install) in one module, while a parallel command surface lives in src/core/cli.ts and a third helper layer in src/cli/schedule.ts (alive — imported at cli/bakin.ts:19) plus src/core/cli/* — four CLI locations total.
deferred.recommendation: Defer but document as the refactor target after the registry cycle work: split per-command modules under src/cli/ (the schedule.ts precedent already exists), keep cli/bakin.ts as a thin dispatcher, and route the two direct-settings call sites through the existing /api/settings endpoint so the CLI is honestly HTTP-only.

deferred.title: Help/usage registry drifts from implementation: `bakin check agent-assets` is documented but rejected; plugin-contributed commands are dispatchable but invisible in help
deferred.evidence: registry.ts:150-151 advertises `bakin check <...|plugin-assets|agent-assets|...>` and `bakin install <...|agent-assets|...>`, but the implementation accepts only 'agent-sync' (cli/bakin.ts:4429, 4439; the unknown-subcommand lists at 4434/4442 also say 'agent-sync'). A user following help gets 'Unknown check subcommand: agent-assets'. This drift is structural: usage strings in registry.ts are maintained by hand, disconnected from the dispatch switch, so nothing fails when they diverge. Conversely, plugin-contributed CLI commands are matched and dispatched at runtime (dispatchPluginCliCommand, cli/bakin.ts:3761-3787, reading contributes.cliCommands from /api/plugins/manifest) but printHelpTui (238) renders only the static CLI_COMMANDS registry — installed plugin commands never appear in `bakin --help`.
deferred.recommendation: Fix the agent-assets/agent-sync strings now. Structurally, make registry entries own their subcommand enums (parser.ts already extracts literal prefixes from usage strings) so dispatch and help share one source of truth, and merge manifest-contributed cliCommands into the help output when the server is reachable.

deferred.title: plugin-settings route writes/reads `<lastPathSegment>.json` without validating the plugin id
deferred.evidence: `extractPluginId` (`:17-21`) takes `segments[segments.length-1]` from `url.pathname` and `getSettingsPath` (`:13-15`) builds `join(getContentDir(), 'plugin-settings', `${pluginId}.json`)`. The PUT handler (`:37-47`) then `writeFileSync`s the request body to that path. No `PLUGIN_ID_RE` validation and no check that the plugin exists in `pluginRegistry` — every other plugin entry point validates the id (e.g. install.ts:536, restore.ts:42). I could not construct a real traversal: Node's URL normalizes `..` path segments away before the handler sees them, and `%2e%2e%2f`/`%2f` stay percent-encoded in `url.pathname` so they become literal filename characters rather than separators, keeping the write inside `plugin-settings/`. The residual risk is writing junk `*.json` settings files for arbitrary/non-existent plugin ids, not an out-of-directory write.
deferred.recommendation: Add the standard `PLUGIN_ID_RE.test(pluginId)` guard (returning 400) at the top of both `get` and `put`, matching the validation every other plugin-id-consuming route already performs. Defense-in-depth and consistency; not an exploitable traversal today.

deferred.title: GitHub plugin installs trust a shipped dist/ that is never rebuilt from the validated source
deferred.evidence: packages/host/src/api/plugins/install.ts:718 calls `buildUserPlugin(targetDir, { trustExistingDist: body.type === 'github' })` for every github install. In packages/host/src/plugin-host/user-plugin-builder.ts:223-229, when `trustExistingDist` is set and the expected dist outputs exist (`trustCompleteDist && clientDistFresh`), the build returns immediately and the plugin's prebuilt `dist/index.js` is what later gets dynamic-imported/activated (install.ts:751 `activateUserPluginDir`). `validatePluginImports` (user-plugin-builder.ts:212) runs against the plugin's *source*, but the bytes that actually execute come from the attacker-supplied `dist/`, which need not correspond to that source. A reviewer who audits a github plugin's source therefore gains no assurance about the code that runs. This is not a privilege escalation over the documented model (installing any plugin runs arbitrary in-process server code by design), but it defeats source-level review as a mitigation and is undocumented.
deferred.recommendation: Either rebuild from source on github installs (drop `trustExistingDist` for non-artifact installs and require a toolchain), or only trust dist/ when it carries verified Whiskit provenance (the artifact path already does this via verifyChecksum/readProvenance). At minimum, document that `bakin plugins install github:...` executes the repo's prebuilt dist, not its source.

deferred.title: Antfly basic-auth password is stored in settings.json and returned unredacted by GET /api/settings, violating the documented secret-isolation invariant
deferred.evidence: The secret-store design explicitly states secrets live in a dedicated ~/.bakin/secrets.json '...separate from the broadcast settings.json so a secret never rides an SSE frame or a settings export' (secret-store.ts:13-17). But the search adapter's basic-auth credential is a settings.json field: SearchAdapterSettings.auth?: { username: string; password: string } (settings.ts:19), persisted through updateSettings into settings.json. server.ts:382 handles GET /api/settings with `jsonResponse(res, 200, getSettings())` — the full settings object, unredacted, including search.settings.auth.password when configured. The same object is what `bakin settings` export reads. Impact is bounded by the threat model (Tailscale perimeter, single operator, the browser is the operator's own), and the field is unset by default (DEFAULT_SETTINGS has no auth), so no live credential is leaking today — but any operator who configures antfly auth gets a credential that contradicts the stated 'never rides a settings export' invariant. Note: logging is clean — settings.ts:445 logs only `keys: Object.keys(partial)`, and the antfly adapter logs only the url, never the password (search.ts connect path).
deferred.recommendation: Move the antfly auth credential out of settings.json into the secrets.json store (or a parallel 0600 file) the same way provider API keys were moved, OR redact secret-shaped fields server-side in the GET /api/settings response. If kept in settings.json for now, add it to a server-side redaction allowlist so the raw password never reaches the browser or a settings export.

deferred.title: Execution ledger stores image-prompt content in idempotency.result_json, contradicting the 'coordination facts only, never content' invariant
deferred.evidence: ledger.ts:15 and the db module both assert the ledger holds 'Coordination facts only — never content.' The idempotency table is `CREATE TABLE idempotency (key, kind, result_json TEXT NOT NULL, ...)` (ledger.ts:113-120). runBilledImageCall (idempotency.ts:152-162) calls `putIdempotent(signature, 'image.'+op, result)` where `result` is the full ExecToolResult. That result is built by imageToolResultFromVersion (tools.ts:415-429), which includes `prompt: (version.prompt ?? req.prompt).slice(0, 500)` (tools.ts:426) — i.e. up to 500 characters of the verbatim image-generation prompt, plus providerText/revised-prompt when present (tools.ts:351). So the ledger persists user/agent prompt content durably (no TTL), which the design says belongs only in markdown/JSON. The promptHash exists precisely so the prompt itself need not be stored. This is content drift, not a credential leak.
deferred.recommendation: Store only coordination/identity fields in the idempotency row needed to return the cached asset (assetId, version, dims, provider/model, promptHash). Reconstruct the full ExecToolResult (including the prompt slice) from the asset manifest on a replay hit, rather than persisting prompt text in result_json.

deferred.title: Dead-code installFromGithub builds a git clone command via shell string interpolation (latent command injection)
deferred.evidence: installFromGithub (plugin-installer.ts:103-128) does `execSync(`git clone --depth 1 ${gitUrl} ${tempDir}`, { stdio: 'pipe' })` (line 116) where gitUrl is derived directly from the `repo` argument with no shape validation or shell escaping (lines 112-114). A repo value containing shell metacharacters would execute arbitrary commands. A grep across the repo (excluding node_modules/dist/test) shows installFromGithub has zero callers — the live HTTP install path is packages/host/src/api/plugins/install.ts, which is properly hardened (parseGithubSource validation, materializeCachedGithubSource using spawn with an argv array, `--` end-of-options, ref validation). So this is currently unreachable, but it is a loaded gun: if any future code wires it up it becomes a real RCE.
deferred.recommendation: Delete src/core/plugin-installer.ts (it is entirely unreferenced dead code superseded by the hardened api/plugins/install.ts), or if any part is still wanted, replace execSync string interpolation with execFile/spawn('git', ['clone','--depth','1','--', url, dir]) and validate the URL shape first.

deferred.title: Status/tone badge class triples (bg-X-500/10 text-X-400 border-X-500/20) hand-rolled per plugin while tasks uses theme tokens
deferred.evidence: The same tinted-badge recipe is re-declared as ad-hoc Record maps in at least four plugins: task-run-history.tsx:34-39 STATUS_CLASS + 41-46 OUTCOME_CLASS (blue/zinc/red/amber/green triples with border), schedule run-history.tsx:46-52 (inline ternary chain producing green/zinc/amber/red triples — semantically the same success/skipped/pending/failed tones as tasks' run history), health-page.tsx:277-280 (ok/warn/error/fixed map, no border), models-page.tsx:45-49 TIER_STYLES (green/blue/purple). Meanwhile plugins/tasks/constants.ts:43-51 STATUS_BADGE_STYLES does it the right way with theme tokens (bg-status-*/10 text-status-* border-status-*/20). The two run-history renderers (schedule and tasks) are the genuinely congruent pair — same Badge variant=outline + tone-triple + timestamp + truncated error row. The rest share only the styling idiom, not semantics.
deferred.recommendation: Document and defer, or do the minimal version: add a `toneBadgeClass(tone: 'success'|'pending'|'error'|'muted'|'info')` util (or a `StatusBadge` component) to the SDK that emits the standard triple from theme tokens, and adopt it in the two run-history components first. Full unification of category-color maps (models tiers, workflow node palette) is not worth forcing — those are domain palettes, not statuses.

deferred.title: HealthCheckResult ok/warn/error constructors copy-pasted into 13+ files with two divergent signatures
deferred.evidence: Identical 3-line ok()/warn()/error() HealthCheckResult constructors are defined privately in 13+ files: the (check, message) variant in plugins/{memory:21-29, assets:24-29, tasks:23-31, schedule:24-32, team:32-40, workflows:30-35}/lib/health-checks.ts, and a (message)-only variant (check name closed over per file) in plugins/health/lib/system-checks/{channel-aliases.ts:6-12, search.ts:11-19, plugin-assets.ts:9-14, restart-recovery.ts:12-18, mcporter.ts:10-18, service.ts:19-27, sync-skill.ts:14-22}. plugins/tasks/lib/health-checks.ts:22 even documents the copy: '// ─── Result constructors (inlined; matches workflows precedent)'. All construct the same { check, status, message, autoFixable } shape from HealthCheckResult in packages/core/src/plugin-types.
deferred.recommendation: Export healthOk/healthWarn/healthError(check, message, opts) from packages/core (next to the HealthCheckResult type, re-exported through @makinbakin/sdk so user plugins get them too) and optionally a makeHealthResults(checkId) curried form for the system-checks style. Sweep the 13 files; ~80 duplicated lines and the 'matches precedent' copy chain disappear.

deferred.title: Host API package routes hand-roll body-parse → safeParse → 400 envelope seven times, with a second error-envelope dialect and message-text status mapping
deferred.evidence: The block `let raw: unknown = {}; try { raw = await req.json() } catch { /* empty body OK */ }` followed by `Schema.safeParse(raw)` and a 400 built from `parsed.error.issues.map((i) => `${i.path.join('.')}: ${i.message}`).join('; ')` is repeated verbatim in packages/dynamic.ts:54-70 and 91-107, agent-packages/dynamic.ts:126-135, 158-168 and 241-249, agent-packages/install.ts:37-41, packages/install.ts:29-36 — seven copies in four files. The plugin route path already centralizes exactly this (empty-body handling, zod parse, issue formatting) in packages/core/src/routing/dispatcher.ts:183-201 + 277-289, but host API handlers bypass it because they're dispatched as raw (req, url) handlers via _adapter.ts. These handlers also use a `{ ok: false, error }` envelope while the dispatcher emits the canonical `{ error, issues }` (packages/core/src/openapi/errors.ts:15-18), and packages/dynamic.ts:82-86 maps HTTP status by regex over error message text (`/still required by/i`, `/not installed/i`) — the pattern the dispatch docs forbid for runtime errors, reinvented here because there's no shared typed-error → status helper.
deferred.recommendation: Either route these handlers through the existing defineRoute/dispatchRoute machinery (it already supports body schemas and emits the canonical envelope), or add a tiny parseJsonBody(req, schema) helper in packages/core/src/routing reused by host handlers. Replace the regex status mapping with typed errors (e.g. a code field on the uninstaller/sync errors) mapped centrally.

deferred.title: Path-param → searchParams injection shim duplicated in catch-all and dispatcher; runs twice per parameterized plugin request
deferred.evidence: The same ~14-line legacy-compat block (inject route :params into a rebuilt Request's searchParams with duplex:'half') exists at [[...path]].ts:219-232 AND dispatcher.ts:111-124. The catch-all builds handlerReq with params injected, then passes the raw params to dispatchRoute, which — because pathParams is non-empty — rebuilds the Request a second time (its `if (!newUrl.searchParams.has(key))` guard skips the sets, but the Request reconstruction still happens). The catch-all copy is fully redundant today. Both blocks exist only for handlers still reading url.searchParams.get() instead of the typed parsed.params: 95 such reads remain in plugins (grep over plugins/*/index.ts + lib), concentrated in team and workflows (team/index.ts alone has 11 manual req.json() calls and dozens of searchParams reads, e.g. team/index.ts:1040,1084,1123); dispatcher.ts:108-110 already marks the shim 'Removed in T20+ once every handler is migrated'.
deferred.recommendation: Delete the redundant injection block in [[...path]].ts:219-232 now (dispatchRoute repeats it). Then finish the acknowledged T20 migration for the two laggard plugins (team, workflows) to declared params/query/body schemas, and remove the dispatcher shim — which also retires their hand-written `if (!x) return Response.json({error},{status:400})` validation (40+ occurrences in team/index.ts alone, e.g. lines 835-836, 909, 963, 1040).

deferred.title: AgentUsage type lives in src/core with a verbatim copy in the health plugin and a plugin-dir-escaping relative import in the team plugin (the only client file in any plugin reaching outside its directory)
deferred.evidence: src/core/agent-usage.ts:12-33 defines AgentUsage (agent/sessionId/model/tokens/cost). plugins/health/components/health-page.tsx:91-110 re-declares a byte-identical `interface AgentUsage` for the `/api/plugins/health/usage` payload (fetched at health-page.tsx:510, consumed at 522). plugins/team/components/overview-tab.tsx:18 instead does `import type { AgentUsage } from '../../../src/core/agent-usage'` — the only client-side import in all 10 core plugins that escapes its plugin directory (verified by grepping plugins/ for ../../../ patterns); it types the `/api/plugins/team/<id>/stats` response (overview-tab.tsx:138-149). Both plugins also expose the same server data independently: plugins/health/index.ts:247 and plugins/team/index.ts:1251 each call getAllAgentUsage(ctx.runtime). An external plugin author could write neither the relative import nor keep the copy in sync.
deferred.recommendation: Export `AgentUsage` from @makinbakin/sdk/types (type-only, zero bundle weight), import it in overview-tab.tsx and health-page.tsx, and delete the health-page copy. Optionally consolidate the two usage routes behind one hook (`useAgentUsage(agentId?)`) later, but the type export alone removes the drift risk and the directory escape.

deferred.title: Tasks plugin hand-rolls workflow wire types that contradict the SDK's published WorkflowInstance, and raw-fetches the workflows plugin API in two dialogs
deferred.evidence: The SDK exports WorkflowInstance with `id` as its key field (packages/sdk/src/types/index.ts:1365-1370), but the actual wire shape uses `instanceId` (plugins/workflows/types.ts:240-241) — so the tasks plugin ignores the SDK type and declares its own local WorkflowInstance/WorkflowDefinition (task-detail-dialog.tsx:147-159, with instanceId/currentStepId/stepStates) plus a WorkflowOption (new-task-dialog.tsx:21-26). The cross-plugin data dependency is hand-fetched: fetch('/api/plugins/workflows/definitions') at new-task-dialog.tsx:40 and task-detail-dialog.tsx:216, plus per-id fetches at task-detail-dialog.tsx:258 and 274. The SDK's loose `[key: string]: unknown` workflow types (sdk types/index.ts:1355-1380) are effectively dead weight no in-repo consumer uses.
deferred.recommendation: Fix the SDK WorkflowInstance/WorkflowDefinition to match the real wire shape (re-export from plugins/workflows/types.ts the way the canonical types already live there), and add `useWorkflowDefinitions()` to @makinbakin/sdk/hooks re-exported from a new plugins/workflows/hooks module — precedent is useNotificationChannels at packages/sdk/src/hooks/index.ts:74. Weight: small fetch hook in the existing sdk-hooks bundle.

deferred.title: Team plugin forks EmptyState — SDK already exports one, and the team plugin uses BOTH variants in the same UI
deferred.evidence: @makinbakin/sdk/components exports EmptyState (packages/sdk/src/components/index.ts:25 → src/components/empty-state.tsx) used by 6 plugins (schedule/job-list.tsx:4, tasks/task-log-table.tsx:8, memory/memory-search-results.tsx:18, workflows/workflows-page.tsx:6, models/models-page.tsx:11, team/team-manager.tsx:6). plugins/team/components/empty-state.tsx is a near-identical fork (same icon→title→description→action structure) that adds a `fillHeight` prop and icon-chip styling; its own comment says 'Keeping a single component means tone + spacing stay consistent' while creating the second component. The fork is consumed by team/agent-detail.tsx:23, heartbeat-tab.tsx:15, and active-context-tab.tsx:20 — so the team plugin renders SDK-styled empty states on one page and fork-styled ones on another.
deferred.recommendation: Add `fillHeight?: boolean` and the icon-chip variant to the SDK EmptyState (src/components/empty-state.tsx), migrate the three fork consumers, delete plugins/team/components/empty-state.tsx. Weight: ~10 lines in the existing sdk-components bundle.

deferred.title: Relative-time and duration formatters re-implemented in 5 plugin files despite formatAge living in @makinbakin/sdk/utils — copy-paste twins already drifting
deferred.evidence: formatAge ('Xm ago'/'Xh ago'/'Xd ago') is exported from @makinbakin/sdk/utils (packages/sdk/src/utils/index.ts:14 → packages/core/src/format.ts:2-11), yet plugins/team/components/heartbeat-tab.tsx:23-36 (formatRelative) and plugins/models/components/models-page.tsx:30-40 (formatRelativeTime) reimplement it almost line-for-line — the forks exist because formatAge lacks seconds granularity, a number-timestamp overload, and a date fallback for old entries. A second family: plugins/schedule/components/run-history.tsx:7-19 (formatTime, 'Today/Yesterday HH:MM') and plugins/tasks/components/task-run-history.tsx:8-22 (relativeTime) are copy-paste twins where the tasks copy has already drifted (it added prior-year handling with an explanatory comment; schedule's copy didn't get the fix). formatDuration is duplicated twice within the tasks plugin alone (task-run-history.tsx:24-30, task-log-table.tsx:160).
deferred.recommendation: Extend formatAge in packages/core/src/format.ts (accept Date|string|number, optional seconds granularity, locale-date fallback past N days), and add formatCalendarTime ('Today/Yesterday HH:MM' with the year fix) and formatDuration to @makinbakin/sdk/utils, then migrate the 5 call sites. Weight: tens of lines in the sdk-utils bundle, shared via #422 splitting chunks.

deferred.title: Core plugin id list maintained in three places and one copy has already drifted (dev.ts omits 'images')
deferred.evidence: build-plugins.ts:19-23 lists 10 plugins (including 'images'); scripts/dev.ts:71-75 lists 9 (no 'images'), so the dev loop never registers a watcher for plugins/images (dev.ts:446-463); scripts/docs/generate.ts:2329 hardcodes a third list (inRepoPluginIds, 10 ids) for OpenAPI route extraction. The dev.ts omission is currently benign because plugins/images has no client.tsx (verified: only index.ts/lib/types.ts/defaults/bakin-plugin.json) and there is no comment explaining the omission — if images ever grows a client, hot-reload silently won't work for it; adding plugin #11 requires remembering all three lists plus the docs list.
deferred.recommendation: Move CORE_PLUGINS into src/core/whiskit (next to the externals contract) or derive it by scanning plugins/*/bakin-plugin.json, and import it in build-plugins.ts, dev.ts, and generate.ts. If the images exclusion in dev.ts is intentional, replace it with a 'has client.tsx' check or a comment.

deferred.title: scripts/docs/generate.ts is a 2,585-line top-level script bundling eight independent generators
deferred.evidence: 2,585 lines (verified via wc), executed entirely as module-level side effects — no main(), with mid-file top-level `await import(...)` (generate.ts:2326-2328) and writeStableFile calls scattered through the tail. It contains at least eight separable concerns: markdown content-block sync (updateGeneratedContentBlocks, :215), hook extraction + reference rendering (:258, :1782), slot extraction (:288), SDK symbol extraction via the TypeScript compiler API (:569-781), CLI reference rendering (:818-1180), OpenAPI document construction (:1182-1508, plus a second typed builder at :2315+ that the comment says 'Replaces the legacy buildOpenApiDocument()' — the legacy _buildOpenApiDocument at :1437 is still present, underscore-prefixed), MCP tool reference (:1669-1780), coverage report (:939), and llms.txt bundle emission (tail). Any failure leaves a partially written docs/.generated tree.
deferred.recommendation: Split into one module per emitted artifact (content-blocks, openapi, cli-reference, hooks, mcp-tools, sdk-reference, llms-bundles) under scripts/docs/, with generate.ts as a thin orchestrator with a main(). Delete the superseded _buildOpenApiDocument path. This also enables the check.ts sharing fix.

deferred.title: Docs hook/slot extraction is line-regex scraping that can silently drift from runtime HookRegistry registrations
deferred.evidence: generate.ts pulls CLI commands, routes, settings, and permissions from the real server modules (imports CLI_COMMANDS from src/core/cli/registry, getAllRoutes from src/core/api-docs, DEFAULT_SETTINGS, PermissionSchema — generate.ts:16-21), so those cannot drift. But hooks and slots are scraped by regex: extractHookRegistrations (generate.ts:262) matches `hooks.register(['"`]name` on a single source line and scans only the next 45 lines for label/summary/hookKind metadata; extractSlotRegistrations (generate.ts:288-307) matches `slot: '...'` only when 'registerSlot' appears within 8 lines. Hooks registered with computed names, via wrapper helpers, or with metadata objects defined elsewhere are silently omitted from the published hooks reference, and nothing in check.ts validates the hook list against the live HookRegistry.
deferred.recommendation: Either register hook metadata declaratively (manifest contributes.hooks, like cliCommands already migrated) and generate from that, or have generate.ts activate plugins against a mock ctx and read the real HookRegistry, mirroring how the typed OpenAPI path already imports plugin route objects directly.

deferred.title: Production exec-tool registry and MCP tool implementations live under scripts/, with a stray npx-tsx debugging CLI
deferred.evidence: scripts/lib/registry.ts is the runtime exec-tool registry (globalThis-backed Map, builds full PluginToolContext with storage/search/runtime facades) imported by production server code: src/core/mcp-server.ts:34 and :44-48 (which also imports scripts/lib/{log-progress,post-channel,get-paths,heartbeat,search-tools} for self-registration), src/lib/plugin-registry.ts:46, src/core/plugin-host/reload-pipeline.ts:39, and packages/host/src/api/exec-tools/[toolName].ts:9. So a directory the repo treats as build tooling (and that this audit's lint/test scopes treat as scripts) ships in the compiled binary's module graph. Separately, scripts/bin/post-channel.ts:1 has shebang `#!/usr/bin/env npx tsx` in a Bun-only repo (tsx is not how anything else runs here) and prints its own warning that it 'bypasses Bakin tracking (no MCP call, no Health metrics, no audit log)'.
deferred.recommendation: Move scripts/lib/* into src/core/exec-tools/ (or packages/core) so the production module graph contains no scripts/ paths, leaving scripts/ purely build/dev tooling. Fix or delete scripts/bin/post-channel.ts (bun shebang, or remove — the MCP tool is the supported path).

deferred.title: Imitation Crab usage-seeding module is bundled into the production binary and activates via a single env var
deferred.evidence: server.ts:815-819: `if (process.env.BAKIN_SEED_USAGE === '1') { import('./dev/imitation-crab/usage-seed').then(m => m.seedMockUsage())... }`. The specifier is a static string, so `bun build --compile` bundles the mock module into release binaries — verified: `strings dist/bakin-darwin-arm64 | grep imitation` shows the embedded source comment `// dev/imitation-crab/usage-seed.ts`. usage-seed.ts imports src/core/usage's recordUsage and fabricates MCP/REST/agent usage entries (fake tool names like bakin_exec_post_discord), so setting BAKIN_SEED_USAGE=1 on a production install pollutes the health dashboard's usage feed with synthetic data. Damage is bounded (the recorder is in-memory), hence P2 rather than P1.
deferred.recommendation: Gate the import on BAKIN_DEV as well (like the hot-reload coordinator at server.ts:827), or move seedMockUsage behind the imitation-crab gateway/dev.ts side so dev/ code is never in the compiled module graph; alternatively have build-binary.ts fail if the bundle contains dev/imitation-crab paths (extend assert-production-assets).

deferred.title: Embedded-assets codegen interpolates paths into string literals without escaping
deferred.evidence: emitManifest builds the generated module with raw template interpolation: generate-embedded-assets.ts:204 `import ${a.varName} from '${spec}' with { type: 'file' }` and :209 `['${a.urlPath}', ${a.varName}],` — neither spec nor urlPath is escaped. A file under packages/host/public/, plugins/*/dist/, or packages/host/src/data/ whose name contains a single quote, backslash, or newline produces a syntactically broken _embedded-assets-static.ts. The failure is loud (the next compile fails), so this is fragility rather than a silent-pass risk; today all walked filenames are build outputs with safe names.
deferred.recommendation: Use JSON.stringify() for both the import specifier and the map key when emitting the module (one-line change each), making the codegen safe for any filename.

deferred.title: Orphaned one-shot scripts with no npm-script or workflow references
deferred.evidence: Checked package.json scripts and all four .github/workflows/*.yml before claiming this. scripts/docs/backfill-manifests.ts: zero references anywhere (grep over scripts/.github/package.json/docs/.claude returned nothing); its header says 'Re-run it any time source registrations change', but nothing documents or wires that. scripts/migration/validate-package.ts: only referenced by its own usage string and one line in .claude/knowledge/agent-packages.md — a manual util living in a 'migration' dir that suggests a completed migration. scripts/release.ts:371-376: main() now unconditionally throws 'Local release publishing has been retired', yet the file still carries the dead CLI surface — parseArgs (:348) and releaseWorkflowUrlFromRuns/ReleaseWorkflowRun (:342, :33) which only served the retired publisher; the file's live role is changelog helpers for prep-release.ts:11-18 and tests.
deferred.recommendation: Delete backfill-manifests.ts if the contributes backfill is complete (the validator catches drift per its own header), or wire it as a docs: npm script. Move validate-package.ts next to the package code it validates or delete. deferred.title: Five ad-hoc recursive directory walkers across scripts with inconsistent ignore rules
deferred.evidence: Each script reimplements recursive walking with different skip lists: generate-embedded-assets.ts:73-90 (walk; skips only .map files), assert-production-assets.ts:13-26 (walkFiles; no skips at all — it walks every plugins/<id> subtree including any node_modules/ that appears, then filters by suffix), source-scan.ts:66-74 (walkFiles; skips node_modules/dist/.astro), check.ts:45-52 (walkMarkdown; no skips), generate.ts:215-225 (inline walk inside updateGeneratedContentBlocks; no skips). None share code, so ignore-rule fixes (e.g. excluding a future plugins/<id>/node_modules) must be discovered and applied five times.
deferred.recommendation: Add a single scripts/lib-build/walk.ts (or use Bun.Glob, already available in the runtime) with explicit ignore options, and migrate the five walkers during the docs-generator split.

cohesion.riskNotes: Entry path is load-bearing three ways: package.json bin maps "bakin" -> ./cli/bakin.ts (package.json:10), the compiled binary's dispatcher dynamic-imports '../../cli/bakin' and destructures { main } (src/core/cli.ts:250), and scripts/instance.ts:155,208 + scripts/instance/sandbox.ts:35 shell out to `bun run cli/bakin.ts` — so cli/bakin.ts must survive as a file exporting main() with the import.meta.main guard (4630-4632). The binary delegation contract is fragile: delegateToSourceCli monkey-patches process.exit to throw DelegatedCliExit (src/core/cli.ts:243-247) and main() deliberately rethrows BakinDelegatedCliExit and /^exit:\d+$/ errors (bakin.ts:4588-4593); extracted command modules MUST keep calling process.exit (not return codes) or the binary's exit-code plumbing and tests like doctor-repair.test.ts (`rejects.toThrow('exit:1')`, line 120) break. All heavy deps (react, ink, src/core/cli/ui/*, onboarding components, whiskit build) are dynamically imported on purpose to keep binary startup cheap (comment 55-57) — the split must not let any new module statically import them into the entry's import graph; conversely the static imports at the top (whiskit publish/artifacts-index lines 8-15, settings line 20, import-export 23-29) already load server-side core on every CLI invocation and should move into their command modules as part of the split. Mutual lazy dependency exists between cli/bakin.ts and src/core/cli.ts (bakin.ts 2698-2699 and 4458 import src/core/cli; src/core/cli.ts:250 imports bakin) — both sides must stay dynamic or the split creates a static cycle. Tests in tests/cli/* mock dependency modules (onboarding components, ui modules, settings) by their own resolved paths and then import { main } — they survive the split as long as the extracted code keeps importing the exact same modules; only relative specifiers change. No registerPlugin/addExecTool/globalThis-HMR state anywhere in this file (verified). One behavioral landmine: cmdLogs ends with `await new Promise(() => {})` and a SIGINT handler (3326-3332) — whatever module owns it inherits a never-resolving promise that would hang any caller that awaits it outside the process-exit flow.

wireChannelApprovals(ctx): the rehydratePendingApprovals call (1565-1573) and the subscribeApprovalResponses handler (1576-1677) rewritten on top of decideGate; owns the unsubscribe handle currently held in module-scope let (81).
registerWorkflowHooks(ctx): the 19 ctx.hooks.register one-liners (1679-1720), importing createValidatedInstance from start-validation so hooks and routes share one implementation.

Imports, settingsSchema/navItems (1292-1305), definePlugin with routes composed as [...definitionRoutes, ...gateRoutes, ...instanceRoutes], activate() reduced to orchestration (registerWorkflowSearch, loadDefaultWorkflows + notification wiring 1457-1480, wireChannelApprovals, registerWorkflowHooks, health checks 1725-1741, registerWorkflowExecTools), lifecycle onReady/onSettingsChange/onShutdown (2024-2067).

redesignOpportunities: Unify the duplicated validation paths and fix the divergence: REST POST /instances/start (index.ts:1260) uses the weak module-scope createValidatedInstance (296-309) whose validateWorkflowForStart (262-294) skips nested-workflow recursion and cycle detection, while the workflows.createInstance hook (1681) and bakin_exec_workflows_start (1802) use the strong activate-scoped version (1500-1563). Keep only the recursive validator; REST starts become stricter (desired).

Collapse the six copy-pasted gate-decision blocks (848-909, 914-973, 1046-1076, 1078-1112, 1593-1627, 1628-1676) into one decideGate service — each repeats approvalRef capture, approve/rejectGate, audit, activity log, indexInstance, triggerDispatch, resolveGateApproval, sendGateDecisionSummary with only the surface ('web'/'channel') and response shape differing. Saves ~250 lines and makes the next decision surface a 10-line wrapper.

Delete the dead/shadowed duplicate helpers: instanceToSearchDoc (200-212 vs 1315-1327), indexInstance (214-224 vs 1446-1455), getGateDescription (226-231 vs 821-826), buildGateAuditPayload (233-249 vs 831-845), getRuntimeAgentNames (251-260 vs 1482-1490), activeGateSettings (95-97 vs 1480). The triple-scope pattern (module / populateWorkflowRoutes closure / activate closure) exists only because route handlers can't see ctx at module load — fix by having handlers use their PluginContextLite parameter or a single ctx accessor instead of the mutable pluginCtx module global (84).

Replace populateWorkflowRoutes(arr: any[]) (444) + the 'as unknown as Parameters<typeof definePlugin>[0]["routes"]' cast (1287) with typed defineRoute[] arrays exported per route module and spread into definePlugin — the any[] mutation pattern defeats the route typing defineRoute exists to provide.
Hoist the response-schema literal repeated verbatim on 18 routes ('responses: { 200: passthroughWf, 201: passthroughWf, 400: errorResponseWf, ... }', e.g. 465, 499, 522) into one shared const.

bakin_exec_submit_step classifies errors by message text — msg.includes('near-duplicate') || msg.includes('rejection') at 1962 — which violates the repo-wide 'never classify by error-message text' rule (architecture-enforced for dispatch). Have lib/runtime.ts throw a typed error with a kind field and switch on that.

gateNotificationSettings exists in two places: the module-scope let (90-94) seeded in activate (1474-1479) AND the notifications module's own store via set/getGateNotificationSettings — activeGateSettings() (95-97) papers over the dual source of truth. Make lib/notifications.ts the single owner with a default.
sharedExtractionCandidates: triggerDispatch (index.ts:412-415) is a verbatim re-implementation of the already-exported triggerDispatch in src/core/task-service.ts:556-559 — and the core one resolves the port via getPort() rather than raw process.env.PORT. Delete the plugin copy and import the core one (or, since plugins shouldn't import src/core directly, expose it via ctx/hook — tasks already imports it).
escapeHtml (index.ts:2106-2113) duplicates scripts/docs/generate.ts:806. A tiny html-escape helper belongs in packages/core (or the SDK) if the gate-decision HTML page stays server-rendered.

The user-definition YAML path helpers (getDefinitionsDir/getUserDefinitionPaths/findExistingUserDefinitionPath/writeUserDefinition, 531-551) duplicate path-resolution knowledge that lib/parser.ts and lib/source-registry.ts already own (the .yaml/.yml dual-extension rule appears again in the search onUnlink handler at 1378-1380) — consolidate in lib/parser.ts or a lib/user-definitions.ts.

formatSchema/formatStepContext (315-409) are generic JSON-schema-to-text and step-context-to-text formatters whose comment says 'migrated from scripts/lib/get-step.ts'; if any other plugin renders schemas for agents, this is SDK material, otherwise keep plugin-local in lib/step-format.ts.
cohesion.riskNotes: Module-load side effects: populateWorkflowRoutes(workflowRoutes) executes at import time (index.ts:1283-1284) and the module is statically imported into the binary via src/lib/plugin-static-imports.ts — route arrays must still be fully built before definePlugin runs, so route modules must be side-effect-light pure builders. Mutable module state crosses the proposed seams: pluginCtx (84) is written in activate (1310) and read by module-scope indexInstance/getRuntimeAgentNames used inside route closures built before activate runs — the split must replace this with the PluginContextLite handlers already receive or a shared ctx accessor module, or routes silently no-op search indexing. unsubscribeApprovalResponses (81) and gateNotificationSettings (90) are similar module-lets referenced by onShutdown/onSettingsChange (2051-2067). Behavior change: unifying validateWorkflowForStart makes REST POST /instances/start reject nested-workflow cycles it previously accepted — tests/plugins/workflows/definitions-crud.test.ts and exec-tools.test.ts exercise these paths and import the plugin default from '@bakin/workflows', which must remain the default export. No import cycles today (index.ts only imports lib/*; lib modules don't import index), but lib/exec-tools.ts and lib/routes/* importing lib/search-sync.ts and lib/gate-decision.ts must not import index.ts back. client.tsx and the SDK re-exports (packages/sdk/src/hooks/index.ts:74-78 → hooks/*) are untouched by this split; this is server-only code, no HMR globals involved.

seams.contents: Pure re-export barrel preserving the current public surface: start, stop, dispatchTasks, dispatchSingleTask, clearDispatchMarker, getDispatchInfo, loadDispatchState, isTaskDispatchEligible, classifyDispatchError, classifyDispatchFailureDetail, formatSanitizedRuntimeFailure, buildDispatchMessage, buildDispatchAssetBlock, buildDispatchLessonBlock, __resetLessonBlockCache, awaitDispatchIdle, getInFlightTurnCount, and the exported types (DispatchEligibility, DispatchContinuationContext, DispatchRosterAgent, ConcurrencyGate). Required because server.ts:37 does `import * as dispatch from './src/core/dispatch'` and three test files mock the whole module path (tests/core/continuation.test.ts:39-40, doctor-delegate.test.ts:42, lifecycle.test.ts:42).

The .dispatch-state.json layer: DispatchState/FailureRecord/SessionDeathState/SessionDeathDiagnosisLite types (lines 167-234), the withStateLock async mutex + stateQueue (453-458), getStateFile/loadDispatchState/saveDispatchState (460-462, 1006-1023), dispatch-marker helpers getDispatchMarkerTaskId/removeDispatchMarkersForTask (478-494), trimDispatched (999-1004), getFailureRecord/cooldownForFailure (464-476), clearDispatchMarker (1274-1280). Single owner of the mutex and the file format.

Taskboard-facing reads and policy: DispatchTask/DispatchTaskSnapshot/DispatchColumns/DispatchEligibilityContext types + emptyDispatchColumns/readDispatchColumns (236-297), isTaskDispatchEligible (299-324), findDispatchTaskSnapshot/taskAlreadyLeftActiveWork (496-507), addTaskLog/tryAddTaskLog/moveTaskToInProgress wrappers (326-333, 509-516). isTaskDispatchEligible is already a pure exported unit with its own tests.

Pure error classification over RuntimeError/RuntimeTurnError: formatDispatchError + MAX_ERR_LEN (87-95), TRANSIENT_CODES + classifyDispatchError (335-362), DispatchFailureKind/DispatchFailureDetail types + classifyDispatchFailureDetail (364-445), formatSanitizedRuntimeFailure (518-533). Zero dispatch state — all pure functions.

The concurrent-dispatch engine: sendDispatchMessage (41-48), claimDispatchRun (66-74), auditDispatchSuppressed (76-85), InFlightTurn registry + getInFlightTurnCount + concurrencyGate (830-874), pendingLadderRedispatches + awaitDispatchIdle (879-894), fireDispatchTurn (901-997). Owns a new scheduleLadderRedispatch() helper so the pending counter (currently mutated from handleSessionDeath at line 720 and read at 887) stays in one module.

The recovery ladder: SESSION_DEATH_REDISPATCH_DELAY_MS + ladder caps (542-552), stripSalvage (554-565), salvageSessionDeathOutput (573-600), handleSessionDeath (616-731), reconcileRejectedDispatch (733-828). The dispatchSingleTask re-dispatch at line 722 must be injected (callback or late-bound setter) to break the cycle with single.ts — see risk notes.

Async prompt-context builders that hit external systems: lessonBlockCache + LESSON_BLOCK_CACHE_TTL_MS/MAX + __resetLessonBlockCache + buildDispatchLessonBlock (102-165), buildDispatchAssetBlock via the assets.listByTask hook (1611-1624). Distinct from prompts.ts because these are async, cached, and audit-emitting; the prompt builders are synchronous string assembly.

Regular-task prompt assembly: mcporterHelpers (1486-1493), sharedExecutionToolDocs (1500-1521), outputDisciplineSection (1532-1542), buildCorrectiveSection (1549-1566), buildDecompositionMessage (1574-1598), DispatchRosterAgent (1600-1603), buildDispatchMessage (1627-1706). All pure string builders.

Workflow-step dispatch as a cohesive unit: dispatchWorkflowTask (1731-1852) + buildWorkflowDispatchMessage (1861-2050). These two are each other's only real coupling partner (the message builder's 9-field stepContext shape is produced only by dispatchWorkflowTask's workflows.getCurrentStep hook call at 1779) — keeping them together avoids exporting that shape.

The periodic cycle: dispatching/dispatchStartedAt/dispatchTimer mutex globals + DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_MS (447-451), dispatchTasks with its two-phase collect-then-fire loop (1025-1263), start/stop (1708-1725), getDispatchInfo (2052-2079, reads the `dispatching` flag so it lives here).

Immediate single-task dispatch: DispatchContinuationContext + dispatchSingleTask (1282-1484), covering kick/subtask/continuation/recovery sources, the recovery-source concurrency-gate task-log special case (1396-1404), and the onSettled usage recording (1467-1481).

redesignOpportunities: ~120 lines copy-pasted between dispatchTasks and dispatchSingleTask: runtime roster + main-agent resolution (1042-1048 vs 1304-1310), completedTaskIds/knownTaskIds set building (1053-1059 vs 1311-1317), eligibility + dangling-dependency logging (1121-1131 vs 1329-1332), failure cooldown/max-retry checks (1137-1152 vs 1342-1352), and the claim→lesson→assets→message→move→audit→fire sequence (1181-1228 vs 1407-1482). Extract one prepareAndFireRegularDispatch() used by both paths; drift already exists — the single path records recordUsage via onSettled (1467-1481) and the workflow-single path records it inline (1369-1386), but the cycle path records no usage at all.

dispatchWorkflowTask takes 9 positional parameters including injected moveTaskToInProgress/addTaskLog functions (1736-1738) that are always the module-local functions or a no-op `async () => {}` (line 1094, to skip the column move for already-inProgress tasks). Replace the fake dependency injection with an options object ({ skipColumnMove: boolean }) on a DispatchContext carrying contentDir/port/settings, which all layers currently thread by hand.

buildDecompositionMessage re-implements its own local `mc` helper (1579-1580) instead of calling mcporterHelpers (1486-1493), defeating the explicit single-source-so-they-cannot-drift comment at 1495-1499. Fix while moving both into prompts.ts.

server.ts:748-749 loads dispatch state, sets serverStart = Date.now(), and discards the object — saveDispatchState is module-private (dispatch.ts:1021) so the write can never be persisted. getDispatchInfo (2057) then baselines nextRun off the STALE serverStart from the previous process. During the split, fold the serverStart stamp into start() or export a markServerStart(contentDir).

saveDispatchState uses a non-atomic writeFileSync (1022); a crash mid-write corrupts .dispatch-state.json and loadDispatchState's catch (1015-1018) silently resets ALL failure records and in-flight ladder state. Write temp-then-rename while the function moves to state.ts.
salvageSessionDeathOutput does `const { mkdirSync } = await import('fs')` (583) even though fs is statically imported at line 5 — pointless dynamic import; just add mkdirSync to the top import.

Double wrapper layering: addTaskLog (326-329) wraps appendTaskLog with a data-arity if/else, then tryAddTaskLog (509-516) wraps addTaskLog with the SAME if/else again plus a catch. Collapse to one tryAddTaskLog.

DispatchTask/DispatchColumns locally re-declare the task-store board shape, forcing `as unknown as { columns: ... }` casts at 295, 497, and 1765. The board type should be imported from the task-store module instead of maintained as a third parallel definition.
sharedExtractionCandidates: mcporter command formatting (`mcporter call bakin-<agent>.<tool> ...`) is built by mcporterHelpers in dispatch.ts (1486-1493) and duplicated as raw template strings throughout src/core/team-context-defaults.ts (lines 34-191, ~20 occurrences with the {{agentId}} placeholder) and src/core/bakin-skill.ts:38. A shared formatter (src/lib or packages/core) would keep agent-facing command docs from drifting between dispatch prompts and the composed AGENTS.md context layers.

classifyDispatchError, classifyDispatchFailureDetail, and formatSanitizedRuntimeFailure (335-445, 518-533) are pure functions over RuntimeError/RuntimeTurnError, which are defined in @bakin/core/adapters/runtime (imported at line 12). They belong in packages/core next to the error types so adapters and the watchdog can reuse the canonical classification instead of growing their own (packages/adapter-openclaw/src/runtime.ts:1275 already does its own `instanceof RuntimeError` branching).

withStateLock (453-458) is a generic promise-chain mutex with no dispatch-specific logic; CLAUDE.md documents the same serialize-writes pattern for asset manifests. A packages/core async-mutex utility would replace at least two hand-rolled copies.
cohesion.riskNotes: Module-level mutable singletons must each end up in exactly ONE module: dispatching/dispatchStartedAt/dispatchTimer (447-449), stateQueue (453), lessonBlockCache (104), inFlightTurns (850), pendingLadderRedispatches (879). There is no globalThis HMR guard (server code is not HMR'd per the dev loop), but a duplicated stateQueue across two modules would silently break the .dispatch-state.json mutex — fireDispatchTurn's settle handlers reload state under withStateLock (927, 965) and MUST share the same lock instance as dispatchTasks/dispatchSingleTask. Import cycle: handleSessionDeath schedules dispatchSingleTask via setTimeout (720-730) while dispatchSingleTask → fireDispatchTurn → reconcileRejectedDispatch → handleSessionDeath; splitting session-death.ts from single.ts requires injecting the re-dispatch function (callback parameter or late-bound setter from index.ts), and the pendingLadderRedispatches counter it increments (720, read by awaitDispatchIdle at 887) must move behind a turns.ts helper. Test mocks target the whole module path — tests/core/continuation.test.ts:39-40 mocks BOTH '../../src/core/dispatch' and '@/core/dispatch', doctor-delegate.test.ts:42 and lifecycle.test.ts:42 mock the relative path — so the barrel must remain the import path used by continuation.ts:15, doctor-delegate.ts:11, and lifecycle.ts:8, or the mocks stop intercepting; internal dispatch/* modules must import each other directly (not via the barrel) to avoid self-cycles. server.ts:37 namespace-imports the module and uses dispatchTasks (360, 807), getDispatchInfo (373), loadDispatchState (748), start (801) — all must survive in the barrel. The execution ledger reads .dispatch-state.json directly for its seq-watermark migration (packages/core/src/execution/ledger.ts:74) — the state file's path and dispatchSeq field are a cross-package contract; do not rename or change format during the split. No registerPlugin/addExecTool/binary-embed concerns: this is pure server core, statically imported, never bundled into plugin client assets.

seams.contents: The pure graph/state model, zero JSX: layout constants NODE_WIDTH/NODE_HEIGHT/Y_SPACING/STANDARD_NODE_STYLE/TRIGGER_NODE_ID/APPEND_NODE_ID/RESERVED_STEP_IDS (lines 111-118), BUILTIN_STEP_LABELS (125-132), stepNodeData (428-449), nextStepId (452-459), defaultStepBody (462-474), cloneStep (476-481), looksLikeLegacyHorizontalLayout / looksLikeLegacyCompactVerticalLayout (483-505), EditorState interface (507-512), seedEdges (607-633), seedState (635-679), deriveNodes (681-726), autoArrangeState (728-741), samePosition/sameMeasurement (743-752). All of these are already pure functions over EditorState + WorkflowDefinition; they import only xyflow types and lib/dagre-layout, so they fit the plugin's existing lib/ convention (lib/dagre-layout.ts, lib/node-renderer-registry.ts are precedents for client-only lib modules). This also makes the legacy-layout heuristics and seed/derive logic unit-testable without jsdom.

Canvas chrome components: RESET_NODE_STYLES (95-109), hasPaletteDragType (121-123), EditorNodeShell + the eight Editor*Node renderers + EditorAppendStepNode + BUILTIN_NODE_TYPES (145-302), InsertableEdge + InsertEdgeData (518-605). NOTE: after the dead-code removal described in redesign opportunities, this module shrinks to ~140 lines (EditorAppendStepNode, InsertableEdge, drag-type guard, reset styles); the 280 estimate is the mechanical move before that cleanup.

WorkflowDetailsDrawer (lines 304-394) — a self-contained controlled drawer with its own name/description state, props-only interface, no closure over editor state. Follows the existing one-component-per-file pattern (node-config-drawer.tsx, step-detail-drawer.tsx are siblings).

A hook owning the copy-dialog state cluster: copyName/copyId/copyIdEdited/copyDescription/copyError/copyFieldErrors/creatingLocalCopy/disableOriginal (lines 780-786), the slugify-on-name-change + clearWorkflowDialogFieldError wiring that is pasted verbatim twice in this file (1687-1707 vs 1732-1747), and the shared POST /api/plugins/workflows/definitions + error-envelope parsing common to handleCreateWorkflowSetup (1253-1299) and handleCreateLocalCopy (1301-1360). The two ManagedWorkflowCopyDialog instances (1667-1714, 1716-1754) stay in the editor but collapse to spreading the hook's props. workflow-detail.tsx (lines 104-141, 455-461) carries a third copy of this exact state machine and should consume the same hook.

Navigation guarding, which is fully generic: RouteNavigationBlocker type (514-516), beforeunload effect (878-886), tanStackRouter.history.block effect (888-908), the document-level capture-phase anchor-click interceptor (910-931), completeExit/cancelExitPrompt/handleDiscardAndExit plumbing (1396-1436), and the 'Unsaved workflow changes' Dialog JSX (1756-1796). Exposed as useUnsavedChangesGuard({ hasUnsavedChanges, onConfirmedExit }) returning { requestExit, dialog }. Nothing in this code knows about workflows.

The WorkflowCanvasEditor component itself: props (396-408), editor state hooks, selection/dirty logic, insertStepAt/handleApply/moveSelectedStep/duplicateSelectedStep/deleteSelectedStep callbacks (811-1149), buildDefinition/postOrPut/saveDefinition/handleSave/handleDelete persistence (1172-1384), and the header + ReactFlow + NodeToolbar + drawer-wiring render (1454-1754). Stays the orchestrator; keeps the '@xyflow/react/dist/style.css' import and the export. If still over target after the above, the header bar (1456-1526) is a clean further cut as canvas-editor-header.tsx (~110 lines), but it closes over enough state that I would not force it.

redesignOpportunities: Shadowed dead renderers: nodeTypes is built as { ...BUILTIN_NODE_TYPES, ...registeredNodeTypes } (line 798-800), and client.tsx:46-53 registers real renderers (nodes/agent-node.tsx etc.) into the registry for the exact same kinds (agent, gate, parallel, output, workflow, createTask, trigger, subflowGroup). The registry spread wins, so EditorNodeShell + EditorAgentNode/EditorGateNode/EditorOutputNode/EditorParallelNode/EditorWorkflowNode/EditorCreateTaskNode/EditorTriggerNode/EditorSubflowGroupNode (lines 153-282, ~150 lines) never render in the running app — only 'appendStep' (not registered) is live, plus the registry-empty unit-test path. Worse, the two renderer sets are visually divergent (EditorNodeShell at 164 vs nodes/agent-node.tsx:22 differ in chrome, and the editor versions silently drop skillDrift). During the split, delete the Editor* duplicates, keep EditorAppendStepNode, and make the editor consume the registry exclusively like workflow-canvas.tsx does (line 325).

Three slugify implementations inside one plugin, two of them divergent: workflow-canvas-editor.tsx:417-425 and workflows-page.tsx:29-36 keep \w chars and cap at 60; workflow-detail.tsx:85-91 strips [^a-z0-9]+ with no length cap. The id a user gets for 'My_Flow Copy' depends on which page they started from. Consolidate into one lib function consumed by all three.

setIsDirty(true) called inside setState updater functions at lines 1098, 1112, 1133 (moveSelectedStep, duplicateSelectedStep, deleteSelectedStep). Updaters must be pure — React StrictMode double-invokes them, and a setState-during-updater is an interleaving hazard. insertStepAt (818) and handleApply (1085) already do it correctly outside the updater; normalize.

Weak typing across the drawer boundary: handleApply takes patch: Record<string, unknown> (1050-1051) and merges with { ...base, ...patch } as WorkflowStep (1062); defaultStepBody ends with as unknown as WorkflowStep (473); duplicateSelectedStep round-trips through Record<string, unknown> (1114-1122). A discriminated WorkflowStepPatch type (or at minimum a typed merge helper in the new lib module) would remove four unsafe casts.

Raw fetch + ad-hoc error envelope parsing embedded in the component: postOrPut (1180-1209), handleCreateWorkflowSetup (1274-1285), handleCreateLocalCopy (1325-1346), handleDelete (1368-1375) each repeat the res.json().catch(() => ({})) + (data.error as string) || 'failed (status)' dance. Extract one typed JSON-request helper when splitting out the copy-form hook.

export type { ReactNode } at lines 1801-1803 leaks a React type re-export from a component module as a strict-build workaround; with EditorNodeShell moving out (or dying), the only ReactNode consumer leaves this file and the hack can be deleted.

The component initializes 20+ useState hooks and then has a 21-line reset effect (855-876) that manually re-seeds every one of them when props change — a classic key-remount candidate: the page wrapper can render <WorkflowCanvasEditor key={initialId ?? 'new'}> and the whole effect disappears.
sharedExtractionCandidates: Unsaved-changes navigation guard (beforeunload + TanStack history.block + capture-phase anchor interception, lines 878-931 + 1396-1436): completely generic and exactly the kind of thing other editing surfaces will need; candidate for @makinbakin/sdk/hooks alongside useQueryState. The anchor-click interceptor exists because TanStack's blocker misses plain <a href> navigation — that workaround deserves to live (and be documented) once, not per-editor.

slugify: besides the three in-plugin copies (workflow-canvas-editor.tsx:417, workflow-detail.tsx:85, workflows-page.tsx:29), plugins/assets/lib/filename-id.ts:16 ships a fourth variant. A single sdk util (or packages/core string util re-exported through the SDK) ends the drift.

Canvas constants and node-data mapping duplicated between editor and viewer: NODE_WIDTH/NODE_HEIGHT/Y_SPACING/STANDARD_NODE_STYLE and RESET_NODE_STYLES exist in both workflow-canvas.tsx:19-35 and workflow-canvas-editor.tsx:95-115; stepNodeData exists in both files (canvas:69-94 handles skillDrift, editor:428-449 does not — same name, divergent behavior). The new lib/canvas-editor-state.ts should become the single home and workflow-canvas.tsx should import from it.

JSON fetch + { error } envelope parsing pattern (postOrPut and friends) recurs in workflow-detail.tsx:189-198 and across other plugin components; a small typed apiRequest helper in @makinbakin/sdk would remove the repeated (data.error as string) casts.
cohesion.riskNotes: The file itself has no module-load side effects — registerPlugin/registerNodeRenderer live in plugins/workflows/client.tsx:34-64, and the only load-time effects here are the '@xyflow/react/dist/style.css' import (line 41) and frozen constants; keep the CSS import in the module that always loads with the editor. The node-renderer registry is module-global mutable state with an HMR teardown in client.tsx:59-64 that sweeps ALL registered kinds (the comment admits a workflows-only assumption); if the redesign removes BUILTIN_NODE_TYPES as a fallback, there is a hot-reload window where the registry is swept and the canvas renders unknown node types — either keep a minimal fallback map or scope the cleanup sweep before deleting the duplicates. The smoke test (tests/plugins/workflows/workflow-canvas-editor.test.tsx) stubs '@xyflow/react' and '@tanstack/react-router' via mock.module by package specifier, so moving code between plugin-internal files is safe, but it asserts public contracts that must survive the split: the 'bakin-workflow-node-selected' className (line 841), the insertable-edge { insertIndex, onInsert, onOpenPalette } data shape, RESERVED_STEP_IDS passed to NodeConfigDrawer, and layout.positions in the PUT payload (buildDefinition, 1172-1178). The component is mounted directly as two page slots ('page:/workflows/new', 'page:/workflows/[id]/edit' in client.tsx:41-42), so its props interface is the public surface — keep WorkflowCanvasEditorProps stable. No import-cycle risk if the new lib module stays component-free (lib/dagre-layout and lib/node-renderer-registry already establish that lib/ never imports components/). Binary build embeds only plugins/workflows/dist/client.js, which is bundled — file count changes are invisible to scripts/build-plugins.ts and embedded assets.

seams.contents: Instance persistence + on-disk state: loadInstance, saveInstance, listInstances (runtime.ts:255-268, 1516-1540), generateId, getInstancesDir, getInstancePath (194-204), and the gate-notified tracking file (isGateNotified/markGateNotified/clearGateNotified + loadNotifiedGates/saveNotifiedGates, 1596-1633). Everything here is JSON-state-on-disk with a contentDir parameter and no workflow semantics.

All board-task side effects: findTaskFromStore/addTaskLogToStore/moveTaskInStore (50-64, the ledger-sync wrapper for #482), moveWorkflowTaskToReview (72-99), reconcilePendingApprovalTaskColumns (101-132), completeTaskViaHooks renamed to completeBoardTask (134-145), createBoardTaskForChild (159-192). This is the only part of the file that imports src/core/task-store and src/core/task-service; isolating it makes the core-boundary crossing one auditable module. Depends on instance-store for listInstances.

System/plugin node execution: failSystemNode (398-419), dispatchCreateTaskNode (421-466), PluginNodeDispatchPayload + dispatchPluginNode (473-542), dispatchReopenedStep (1411-1437). dispatchCreateTaskNode's call back into completeStep (line 454) must be broken — either keep it as a dynamic import (the file already uses that pattern at lines 138 and 434) or inject a completion callback.

Read-only query surface (information gating): resolveAgent + getStepOwner (365-392), StepContext + getCurrentStep + buildStepContext (546-729), authorizeWorkflowToolUse (740-791), getActiveAgents (1550-1592). None of these mutate instances; engine and gates import from here, never the reverse — no cycle.

The mutually-recursive mutation core, kept together deliberately: createInstance (276-359), completeStep (796-888), propagateChildCompletion (895-953), advanceWorkflow (966-1097), cancelInstance (1490-1511), plus a new shared finalizeWorkflowCompletion helper extracted from the triplicated completion epilogue. createInstance ↔ advanceWorkflow ↔ propagateChildCompletion call each other recursively (341, 1035, 945) — splitting them would manufacture cycles.

Human-gate operations: ApproveGateOptions/RejectGateOptions/ReopenFromStepOptions/GateDecisionRecord types (1101-1138), approveGate (1143-1225), rejectGate (1231-1341), resolveReopenStep (1343-1362), resetWorkflowFromStep (1364-1409), reopenFromStep (1439-1484). Depends one-way on engine (advanceWorkflow, propagateChildCompletion), step-context (getCurrentStep), node-dispatch (dispatchReopenedStep), task-bridge, and instance-store.

Becomes a pure re-export barrel of the current public surface (createInstance, loadInstance, saveInstance, getCurrentStep, completeStep, approveGate, rejectGate, reopenFromStep, listInstances, getActiveAgents, authorizeWorkflowToolUse, reconcilePendingApprovalTaskColumns, isGateNotified, markGateNotified, clearGateNotified, cancelInstance, and the exported types). cohesion.riskNotes: Lowest-risk split candidate in the codebase: the file is 100% `export interface`/`export type` declarations with only `import type` at the top (verified lines 1-1129) — zero runtime exports, zero module-load side effects, no registerPlugin/addExecTool/globalThis state, and nothing emitted into vendor bundles or the compiled binary (type-only code erases). Main hazards: (1) Import surface — 139 files reference plugin-types, 95 via the '@bakin/core/plugin-types' deep export declared at packages/core/package.json:31; keeping plugin-types.ts in place as a barrel (`export type * from ...`) makes the split zero-churn for importers. Use `export type` re-exports specifically, or Bun/isolatedModules will emit runtime re-export statements for type-only modules. (2) The bidirectional type-only dependency with routing/types.ts (plugin-types.ts:9 vs routing/types.ts:14) must be cut in the right order — move the service types OUT first, then point routing/types.ts at the new leaves; a careless split that leaves routing/types importing the barrel while the barrel imports routing/types preserves the cycle. (3) Any contract change made here (PluginManifest consolidation, HookAPI any-removal) does NOT propagate to external plugin authors because packages/sdk/src/types/index.ts is a deliberate fork — the SDK copy must be updated in the same commit or the existing drift worsens. (4) Internal core consumers import with relative paths ('../plugin-types' from storage/markdown-adapter.ts:7, events/event-bus.ts:5, hooks/hook-registry.ts:9, docs/route.ts:1, routing/types.ts:14) — those five need path updates or rely on the barrel staying at the same path.

Today this is guaranteed because the plugin import is dynamic inside beforeAll (routes.test.ts:152); the harness must be statically imported at the top of each new test file (its module-top mock.module calls then run first) and the plugin import must STAY dynamic — converting it to a static import would race the mocks. mock.module relative specifiers resolve from the calling file, so the harness must sit in tests/plugins/tasks/ (same depth) or the '../../../src/core/...' specifiers silently miss. The two search side-effect tests use fire-and-forget 20ms setTimeout waits (lines 1537, 1552) — already timing-sensitive; co-locate them with their parent route describes rather than giving them their own file. cohesion.riskNotes: The source has load-bearing module side effects that every resulting file must respect. (1) globalThis singletons: src/lib/plugin-registry.ts:1604-1608 stores the registry on __bakinPluginRegistry and line 239 stores the hook registry on __bakinHookRegistry, both captured into module-level consts at first evaluation — under the default non-isolated `bun run test` all split files share one live instance, so each file MUST keep the _resetForTests() + getHookRegistry().clearAll() beforeEach and the registerCorePlugins({}) afterEach (corePluginTable is module-level mutable state, source lines 85-90, cleared by _resetForTests at 1593). (2) __bakinAppServices seeding (test lines 194-199) is how getAppServices() resolves to mock adapters; omitting it in any split file routes context construction at real adapters. (3) mock.module overlays are process-global in shared-global runs — keeping all overlays in ONE harness module imported by every split file (rather than copy-pasting) guarantees identical overlay shapes regardless of file execution order; the logger/audit mock-fn instances must be cleared in beforeEach to avoid cross-file assertion bleed. (4) Ordering constraint: BAKIN_HOME is set in beforeEach BEFORE the dynamic `await import('@/lib/plugin-registry')` (test lines 183 vs 218) — the source's import graph reaches plugins/workflows registries (source lines 29-31) and the lockfile module; the harness must preserve set-env-then-import ordering. (5) Do NOT add the canonical packages/core/src/content-dir mock to the user-plugins file: the lockfile-version test (lines 711-742) depends on the REAL packages/core resolver (lockfile.ts:20 imports '../content-dir') honoring BAKIN_HOME after resetContentDir(); the runtime guard at packages/core/src/content-dir.ts:41-53 is the leak backstop. (6) The afterEach globalThis '__' sweep (244-248) currently deletes unrelated singletons such as __bakinBroadcast if set by earlier files — narrowing it during the split is a behavior change to verify with a full non-isolated `bun run test`, not just per-file --isolate runs. (7) Fixture plugins use `global.__*` side channels and real dynamic import() of temp-dir CJS files — keep fake plugins under tempDir/fake-plugins/ (NOT tempDir/plugins/) or loadUserPlugins double-loads them (documented at test lines 268-270).
